    RN-103 — O binding de agente é POR PROJETO, não mais global

    Até a FASE 23, scope = 'agent' guardava um SLUG global (scope_id = 'qa'), e PUT /projects/:id/agent-bindings/:slug recebia :projectId na rota e o DESCARTAVA de propósito — escolher o modelo do Arquiteto na tela de um projeto mudava o modelo dele em TODOS os projetos. Isso deixou de se sustentar quando a área virou padrão herdável (RN-102): a área é por projeto, e um binding de agente global ACIMA de um padrão por projeto faria o mesmo agente resolver modelos diferentes só onde existisse área — e faria "voltar a herdar" apagar uma decisão que alcançava projetos que ninguém está olhando.

    A saída foi tornar agent por projeto também, e não rebaixar a área para abaixo do agente: scope_id de agent e de area virou COMPOSTO — <projectId>:<slug do agente|chave da área> — em vez de inventar uma tabela nova só para guardar um projeto por binding. UUID de projeto e slug de agente nunca contêm :, o que torna o primeiro : um separador não ambíguo; a leitura corta nele, e não em todos, para um slug com : (nenhum existe hoje, mas nada impede) não virar três pedaços.

    scope_id sem o projeto (o formato antigo) é RECUSADO na escrita, não aceito e ignorado: gravá-lo criaria um binding que a cascata nunca mais encontraria — invisível, e não um erro. A migração 0040 espalha cada binding de agente global existente para uma linha por projeto (preservando o que cada projeto resolvia antes da mudança) e apaga o formato antigo; é ESPALHAR e não apagar porque a linha global nunca guardou informação de a quem "pertencia" — inventar um projeto dono seria inventar dado que não existia.

    RN-106 — git push, PR and deploy do not go out through the terminal — even within the project scope

    REVISED by RN-418 (ADR 0102, GLOBAL decision of the product owner): the deny this record describes became an ABSOLUTE CEILING (unconditional require_approval) — the rest of this entry is history, faithful to what held until the revision.

    Inside the project container the agent is free (ADR 0065): the verb allowlist of ADR 0055 does not converge (findings Z and AD — verb, form and invocation are distinct spaces), and the way out is the wall, not a longer list. But three effects cross the wall and reach the world, and the user's decision was verbatim: "agente livre para o que quiser desde que não seja comandos de git ligado ao deploy e ao PR — estas ações ainda devem ser humanas".

    decide() recognizes git push, git remote add/set-url, git merge, the provider CLIs (gh pr create, gh pr merge, glab mr create/merge, releases and workflow dispatch) and the common deploy commands (kubectl apply, helm upgrade, terraform apply, docker push, npm publish, ...) by token PREFIX, ignoring global flags in between (git -C /tmp push matches). Any segment of the compound command that matches is deny — not require_approval: "always allow" writes the pattern into allow, and one click would be enough for the second door to stay open forever. deny beats allow at any stage, and it is applied BEFORE any permissive stage in decide().

    Denying does not take power away from the agent: the message redirects to the TYPED action (git_push, git_merge, pr_open) — which is born a proposed_action, has its own minimum role and records in the event log what was pushed and where. It is the path the dev agent already uses (agent_io.ex proposes git_push); what changes is that it is now guaranteed by deny, not just agreed by convention.

    • Where: apps/api/src/domain/actions/external-effect.ts, apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts ("FRONTEIRA DO CONTAINER" block)
    • Test: apps/api/test/domain/actions/external-effect.spec.ts, apps/api/test/domain/actions/decide.spec.ts (describe "a fronteira do container")
    • Edge case: the boundary does NOT override the merge lock on a protected branch (RN-014, always manual) nor the path scope (RN-095/ADR 0055) — the three rules coexist, each one vetoing for a different reason.

    RN-109 — The workspace folder name is frozen at creation, and an old project keeps the UUID

    A project's physical folder in PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT was the bare UUID — unreadable when opened on disk. projects.workspace_dir_name (NOT NULL, UNIQUE) started storing the real name: <slug>-<8 chars do id> for a NEW project (workspaceDirNameFor in apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.ts), generated in code — the id is born from crypto.randomUUID() in CreateProjectUseCase, not from Postgres's defaultRandom(), because the folder name needs the id BEFORE the insert. The 8 characters follow the same convention as the session label (apps/web/src/lib/session-label.ts).

    The name is FROZEN at creation time and never recomputed: UpdateProjectUseCase allows editing the slug later, and that does NOT touch workspace_dir_name — renaming the physical folder, with a working tree and agent worktrees possibly open, is a real risk the decision avoids by construction, not by the caller's discipline.

    A project created BEFORE this migration (0042) kept the physical folder it already had: the backfill writes workspace_dir_name = id for every existing row — the same value that was already true on disk — and NEVER renames any directory. A BEFORE INSERT trigger (projects_workspace_dir_name_default_trg) applies the SAME fallback (id::text) to any insert that arrives without the field — a safety net for whoever forgets to write it (never the main path, which always writes it explicitly), and what keeps the dozens of existing test fixtures, which do not know this concept, working without needing to rewrite each one.

    Path derivation from the name (projectScopeRoot, RN-092/RN-075) started receiving workspace_dir_name instead of the raw projectId — same charset validation, same purity. The engine reads the SAME column (Engine.Projects.Project.workspace_dir_name/1) to resolve Engine.Actions.Workspace.workspace_dir/1, never recomputing the name from the id: the two derivations (api and engine) are, in practice, the same read against the same database — that is what guarantees RN-075 (terminal scope) and RN-092 (code reading) keep pointing to the SAME folder the engine really uses.

    RN-114 — Os quatro segredos irmãos do GIT_OAUTH_STATE_SECRET também não sobem em produção com o valor de exemplo

    O ADR 0059 fechou o padrão para GIT_OAUTH_STATE_SECRET e deixou declaradamente aberto que o mesmo modo de falha valia para quatro segredos irmãos, todos com default de desenvolvimento no docker-compose.prod.yml: AUTH_JWT_SECRET, BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN, CREDENTIALS_MASTER_KEY e SECRET_KEY_BASE. Esta RN fecha os quatro, replicando exatamente a mesma regra — não é decisão nova, é a mesma decisão aplicada aos irmãos.

    Em produção (NODE_ENV === 'production'), cada resolutor derruba o boot quando a variável está ausente/só com espaços, é igual ao literal de exemplo do repositório (que é público — está no .env.example), ou tem menos de 16 caracteres. Fora de produção o default de desenvolvimento continua valendo, porque docker compose up sem .env tem que funcionar.

    • AUTH_JWT_SECRET — deriva o par Ed25519 que assina o access token. Com o default público, qualquer um forja um access token válido.
    • BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN — autentica o tráfego interno api ↔ engine. Com o default público, qualquer um chama as rotas /internal/* sem passar pelo EngineServiceGuard.
    • CREDENTIALS_MASTER_KEY — embrulha os DEKs que cifram as credenciais do usuário (chaves de LLM, tokens de git). Com o default público, qualquer um decripta o acervo. Fora de escopo aqui: qualquer mecanismo de rotação — esse já existe (CREDENTIALS_MASTER_KEY_PREVIOUS + src/scripts/rewrap-deks.ts) e não muda; esta é só a checagem de BOOT.
    • SECRET_KEY_BASE (engine) — já derrubava o boot sem a variável (runtime.exs, bloco :prod, boilerplate padrão do Phoenix). O defeito real não era falta de checagem no Elixir: era o docker-compose.prod.yml suprir o literal público como fallback, o que fazia a variável chegar sempre DEFINIDA e mascarava o raise que já existia. A correção aqui foi só remover o fallback do compose — nenhuma linha de Elixir mudou.

    Vale a mesma razão do ADR 0059 para rejeitar o literal, e não só o vazio: o docker-compose.prod.yml supria os quatro literais como fallback, então no caminho real de erro as variáveis estavam definidas — uma verificação de "não vazia" passaria por cima do defeito inteiro.

    • Onde: apps/api/src/infrastructure/security/auth-key-material.ts (passphraseAtual), apps/api/src/infrastructure/security/service-token.ts (tokenDeServicoAtual) e apps/api/src/infrastructure/security/envelope-encryption.service.ts (EnvelopeEncryptionService, checagem no construtor) — os dois primeiros chamados no boot em apps/api/src/main.ts, o terceiro exercitado quando o NestFactory.create monta o grafo de providers. SECRET_KEY_BASE em apps/engine/config/runtime.exs (inalterado) com o fallback removido de docker/docker-compose.prod.yml

    RN-127 — ref/path da aba Code recusam chegar como ARRAY, não só como caminho fora do escopo

    @Query('ref') ref?: string e @Query('path') path?: string (code.controller.ts) extraem o valor cru sem DTO/class-validator no meio, e o ValidationPipe global (main.ts) não ajuda: ele pula tipo primitivo nativo (String) por desenho do Nest, então nada intercepta ref/path antes de chegarem como argumento de método. O Express entrega ?ref=a&ref=b como array, não string — a anotação string do TypeScript só existe em compile-time.

    Um array escapava das DUAS checagens que a RN-095 já fazia tratando o valor como string: ref.includes('..') tem semântica de ELEMENTO EXATO (não substring) em array, e REF_VALIDO.test(ref) chama .toString() no array antes de casar — um valor como ['x/../y'] continha .. e ainda assim passaria pelas duas.

    garantirQueryEscalar(valor, criarErro) recusa o array ANTES de qualquer outra checagem, num lugar só, reusado pelos DOIS pontos que tratavam query como string: caminhoDeRepositorioContido (mesmo arquivo da RN-092/095) e ReadProjectCodeUseCase.alvo (ref). O erro concreto (CaminhoForaDoEscopoError ou BadRequestException) é decidido por quem chama, passado como fábrica — a função central não decide o tipo de erro, só a forma da checagem.

    O caminho feliz não muda: todo ref/path legítimo já era string.

    RN-128 — sessionId/projectId/agent/agentId are validated BEFORE becoming a URL segment of the internal request to the engine

    HttpApiToEngineClient interpolates these values in a template string to build the /internal/* URL — with no DTO/class-validator in between, just like RN-127: they come from @Param/session lookup without a validation pipe at some point of the chain, and nothing guarantees their shape before interpolation. A malicious value could inject an extra path segment or characters that break the built URL — the EngineServiceGuard authenticates the CALLER (RN-035), it does not CHECK what the caller sends in the URL.

    garantirSegmentoDeUrlInterna reuses the same width as NOME_DE_PASTA_VALIDO (RN-092/109) — hex, hyphen and underscore, 1 to 64 chars — and is called in TWO places, covering ALL the methods that interpolate an id in a URL, not only the ones CodeQL reported:

    • inside postCommand, which most methods already use (startAgent, sendAgentMessage, confirmReadiness, cancelAgentTurn, offerInfraHandoff, invalidateInstructions, startExecution, acceptParallelization, rearmDevAgent, reviseStory) — the caller lists the (nome, valor) tuples it already interpolated into the path, and postCommand validates ALL of them before building the request;
    • directly in reanalyzeSession/runAnamnese, which do not go through postCommand (they need to distinguish 503 from a transport failure) and that is why they were the only two points CodeQL reached.

    The happy path does not change: sessionId/projectId are always a UUID from the database, and agent/agentId are always a short slug.

    RN-135 — Activating execution closes the CHAT session that originated the request

    ActivateExecutionUseCase always resolved the EXECUTION session (findActiveExecutionSession, or created a new criativa one), but never transitioned the CHAT session the click on "activate execution" came from — the Dev Lead/PO conversing in a separate session. It stayed active forever, even with execution already running on its own in another session, and kept showing up as an open conversation in the list.

    execute() gained originSessionId, optional and last — an old caller (today only activation from Overview, with no session context) keeps working IDENTICALLY, closing nothing. When passed, at the END of the method (after everything else has happened: module_map, areas, autonomy, startExecution, execution.activated):

    • never closes the execution session itself — if originSessionId equals the session that just received execution.activated, closing is skipped, because closing it would destroy the process the dev agents just gained;
    • only closes what's active — the same caution as decide-bootstrap-plan.use-case.ts#fecharSessao, nothing to do if the session no longer exists or is no longer open;
    • reuses GetSessionPendingWorkUseCase (RN-073) — the SAME guard that holds off closing on inactivity heartbeat: an offered handoff, a pending proposed_action, or an agent working with no subsequent idle prevent closing;
    • goes through closing before closed — the state machine (active -> closing -> closed) doesn't allow the direct jump.

    A failure or pending state here NEVER propagates to whoever called execute(): the ativação da execução já aconteceu e é o efeito principal; fechar o chat de origem é um efeito colateral best-effort.

    RN-139 — The Executors tab reads the CURRENT execution session, never the project's most recent one

    ProjectExecutorsTab fetched the dev agent/QA events by the session that useLatestSession returned — the project's one with the most recent createdAt, without filtering by kind nor requiring execution.activated. It worked only by coincidence: the execution session tends to be the newest. As soon as any session is born after it — a new ideation, a consultative chat — the tab starts looking at that new session, empty of execution events, silently: no hint on screen said which session was being displayed.

    The correct read already existed in the backend: findActiveExecutionSession (SessionRepository) — the most recent active session that carries execution.activated — but it was only used internally by ActivateExecutionUseCase to decide whether to reactivate or create. The fix exposes the SAME criterion over HTTP, instead of duplicating it in the front:

    • GET /projects/:projectId/execution/session (role:viewer) returns the current session or null — it never infers from the most recent;

    • ProjectExecutorsTab swaps useLatestSession for useActiveExecutionSession (a new hook over the route above) as the source of the session the whole tab reads;

    • the tab header always shows WHICH session is being displayed — its label (hashtag + name) linking to SessionPage, or "Nenhuma execução ativa" when null — never implicit again. The three states of RN-088 apply to the session fetch itself: loading, error (with trace_id) and empty (null) are three distinct renders, never an if (!sessão) return null that collapses them.

    RN-143 — A read-only git subcommand is only allowed anchored by the flag that makes the read unambiguous, never by the bare verb

    Querying a real execution's database, dev agents burned dozens of manual approvals on exploration subcommands — git branch -a, git remote -v, git worktree list, git show origin/dev --stat, git log --all --oneline --graph, git for-each-ref, git ls-tree -r origin/dev --name-only, git config user.name — none covered by RN-068, which only allowed git status/diff/log (with no extra flags). Since prefix-by-token matching requires EVERY segment of a composite command to be in allow, a long exploration chain fell entirely into require_approval the moment ONE of these subcommands showed up in the middle.

    DEV_TERMINAL_ALLOW_PATTERNS gained git branch -a/-r/-v/--list/--show-current, git remote -v/git remote show, git worktree list, git show, git for-each-ref, git ls-tree, git rev-parse, and git config --get. git log didn't need a new pattern: matching is already by token PREFIX (extra trailing tokens are allowed), so Terminal(git log) already covered git log --all --graph --oneline --decorate.

    The caution here is the same one RN-068 already shows for ls/lsof, applied to verbs with a MUTATING sibling that accepts the same truncated form of the pattern. Terminal(git branch) would match git branch -D nome (deletes) just as much as git branch nome-nova (creates) or git branch alone — the pattern doesn't see what comes AFTER the prefix it checked. That's why none of the four verbs with a mutating form (branch, remote, worktree, config) was admitted by the bare verb; each was ANCHORED by the flag that makes the read unambiguous regardless of anything that follows it:

    • git branch — anchored on -a/-r/-v/--list/--show-current, never the verb alone; -D/-d/-m/-M (delete/rename) and a bare branch name (create) stay out.

    • git remote — anchored on -v and show (which only accepts a remote name afterward, always a read); add/remove/set-url stay out.

    • git worktree — anchored on list; add/remove/prune stay out.

    • git config — only --get was admitted, because it's the only flag git itself guarantees is a read regardless of what follows (a key, or a key + value pattern). git config user.name/git config user.email WITHOUT --get were deliberately left out: a second token after the key (git config user.name "new value") is a WRITE, and prefix matching doesn't distinguish "no more tokens" from "one more token" without inventing a new argument-counting parser — the same limitation that already blocks a bare git branch. --global/--system were never anchored.

    RN-146 — agent.response carries the name of the model that generated the response

    The model name only existed in token_usage, with no link to the specific agent.response event it produced — SessionPage.tsx showed the FIXED string "modelo" next to the agent's name, never the real name.

An event WRITTEN before this change does not have the key (undefined), and a turn whose api resolved no model writes null — both degrade to the generic label "modelo", never to undefined/null on screen; the same pattern that text === '' already uses for a response prior to RN-059.

    RN-149 — The Container level of the C4 diagram is derived from the module_map, never retyped by the model

    create_c4_diagram (a new Arquiteto tool) generates the two Mermaid syntaxes of the C4 diagram (Context + Container, Simon Brown's model). The tool call carries only system_name/system_description/actors — the modules and the Container-level dependencies are NOT part of the input: the use case fetches the project's CURRENT module_map (ModuleMapRepository.findCurrent, the same read as GetArchitectureUseCase) and derives the Container level from it, with the SAME names and dependencies that create_module_map already validated without cycles.

    The obvious alternative — letting the model describe the modules again in the diagram's tool call, as it already does for create_module_map — was discarded on purpose: a second place where the model writes "the modules are X, Y, Z" is a second place where that list can diverge from the first, and the divergence would be SILENT — nothing would refuse a diagram with a module that no longer exists in the real map. Deriving from the repository closes that divergence by construction: the diagram can become OUTDATED if the module_map changes later (re-emitting is generating again, without a lock — see ADR 0068), but it never LIES about what existed at the moment it was generated.

    Without a current module_map, create_c4_diagram is refused with 400 — there is no Container level without modules to draw, and the error message instructs the Arquiteto to call create_module_map first (RN-061: the refusal comes back through the tool-result, with the whole reason).

    The artifact.c4_diagram artifact is versioned in the event log without a table of its own — the same design as artifact.project_image (ADR 0065): the current one is the one with the highest version, and revising is generating again, never overwriting.

    RN-153 — "Auto mode": the ApprovalCard turns on autonomy for ANY future action of an agent

    Revised by RN-603 (ADR 0167): decide() started receiving also the ORIGIN of the autonomy, and auto mode (the wildcard in auto_approve) no longer goes through the path scope ceiling. What follows below about decide() "not changing" describes the original design.

    Before this RN, agent_autonomy only knew how to grant autonomy per (projeto, agente, TIPO de ação) — one row per type, upsert of ONE rule at a time (SetAgentAutonomyUseCase, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/set-agent-autonomy.use-case.ts). Trusting an agent broadly required one row per type — terminal, write_file, pr_open… — and a new type was born without a rule, back to require_approval.

    "Auto mode" is the special value actionType: "*" in the SAME table and the SAME endpoint (PUT /projects/:projectId/agent-autonomy) — it is not a new mechanism, it is the existing column (agent_autonomy.action_type, free text, no enum nor FK — apps/api/src/db/schema/agents.ts) accepting one more value. The wildcard means "autonomy for any action type of THIS agent" and is resolved in DrizzleAgentAutonomyRepository.findMode (apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/agent-autonomy.repository.ts): it fetches the SPECIFIC rule and the wildcard in the same query, and the specific one always wins — writing terminal: deny with "*": auto_approve already on keeps denying terminal for that agent, and releasing the rest. decide() (apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts) does not change: it receives the PermissionPolicy already resolved in ctx.autonomyMode, exactly as before the wildcard existed — that is why the absolute ceilings hold without needing to know that "auto mode" exists (see RN-154).

    The ApprovalCard (apps/web/src/components/ApprovalCard.tsx) gains the "Modo automático" button next to "Sempre permitir", visible only when: (a) the action is pending, (b) whoever proposed it is an AGENT (actor.kind === 'agent' — there is no agent autonomy to grant to a user) and (c) the caller (ProjectApprovalsTab.tsx/SessionPage.tsx) has already confirmed the maintainer/owner role in the workspace — the same requirement as the endpoint (@RequireRole('maintainer'), unchanged). The onActivateAutoMode prop is undefined for whoever lacks the role — the card HIDES the button instead of showing it disabled, and the check lives in the caller, not in the card (a presentational component, with no query of its own).

    Turning it off reuses the manual/auto toggle the agent card already had (Fase 8d) — no new screen. AgentTeamGrid.tsx starts looking for the agent's wildcard rule BEFORE the representative one (autonomyActionTypeFor): if it exists, the card's toggle reflects and edits the WILDCARD, no longer the representative type — turning off is writing the same wildcard as require_approval, and the toggle on the agent card is exactly that "turn off".

    • Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/agent-autonomy.repository.spec.ts (precedence specific > wildcard; the wildcard is per agent; turning off is rewriting the wildcard as require_approval), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/propose-action.use-case.spec.ts (auto mode auto-approves a common action WITHOUT hitting permissions.json; a specific rule in deny beats the wildcard), apps/api/test/interfaces/http/actions/agent-autonomy.controller.spec.ts (PUT/GET still require maintainer; the DTO accepts "*" and refuses a string outside the list), apps/web/src/components/ApprovalCard.test.tsx (button disappears without onActivateAutoMode; click calls the callback; the note explains the ceilings that keep asking for a decision)

    RN-154 — The three absolute ceilings keep blocking EVEN with "auto mode" on

    Revised by RN-603 (ADR 0167): the ceilings listed here remain in force in auto mode; what stopped holding for it was the PATH SCOPE ceiling (ADR 0055), which was never on this list.

    The design of "auto mode" (RN-153) is deliberately incapable of piercing the three ceilings that already existed in decide() — they are applied LAST, over current.policy, without looking at where the permissiveness came from (agent_autonomy with a specific type, wildcard, or permissions.json — the function never knew how to distinguish the origins, and still does not):

    1. Merge into a protected branch (git_merge with target in dev/qa/rc/main, RN-006) — the merge lock (isProtectedBranch) downgrades auto_approve to require_approval always, even with "*": auto_approve on for the agent.
    2. instruction_patch (RN-007) — changing another agent's instruction requires the human to see the diff; auto mode does not change that.
    3. parallelize/raise_max_parallel (RN-086) — raising the parallelism ceiling, or asking for more agents above it, remains the user's decision; an agent with auto mode on cannot self-grant more spending power.

    The proof is by CONSTRUCTION, not case by case: since the three ceilings check only current.policy === 'auto_approve' — never the origin —, and "auto mode" can only reach current.policy === 'auto_approve' through the SAME path that a specific agent_autonomy rule already used (ctx.autonomyMode), the ceilings that already contained agent_autonomy keep containing the wildcard without needing new code. The real risk was not the ceiling — it was someone, when generalizing agent_autonomy to accept "*", inserting the wildcard check BEFORE the ceilings and reopening the door; that is why AGENT_AUTONOMY_ALL_ACTIONS was resolved entirely in the REPOSITORY (before decide() runs), and decide() itself gained no new line — only enough to have no place where the wildcard could pierce.

    • Where: apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts (the three ceiling blocks, lines ~207–258, unchanged by this feature)
    • Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/propose-action.use-case.spec.ts ("auto mode NÃO auto-aprova merge em branch protegida", "... instruction_patch", "... parallelize/raise_max_parallel" — all three with agent_autonomy "*" written as auto_approve and the verdict remaining require_approval)
    • Origin: design constraint confirmed by the user when asking for "auto mode" — the three ceilings are the guarantee that cannot regress

    RN-155 — timeline ordering uses the proposed_action.created link, never the raw action.seq

    RN-169 — The project chooses where the code lives: Local or Container

    REVISED by RN-421 (ADR 0104): workspace_mode/local became an execution_mode of THREE values (container/mounted/runner, migration 0048) — the rest of this entry is history, faithful to what held until the revision.

    A project is born with a workspace mode (projects.workspace_mode, migration 0043), and it is what decides where the scope root is derived from:

    • container (DEFAULT, and the behavior that always existed): the folder MANAGED by the product, join(PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT, workspace_dir_name) (RN-109);
    • local: a folder OF THE USER, at the absolute path of projects.workspace_path.

    The pair is tied by a CHECK in the database ((workspace_mode = 'local') = (workspace_path IS NOT NULL)), and not only by the use case: the column is read by TWO processes (api and engine) and written by seed/backfill scripts that do not go through it. local without a path would be a terminal scope pointing nowhere; container with a path would be a second source of truth waiting to diverge from the first.

    The derivation remains unique — projectScopeRoot started receiving the location ({workspaceDirName, workspaceMode, workspacePath}) and picks the branch; none of the four consumers (RN-092) gained validation of its own. The engine resolves the same locator in the QUERY (folder name in container, absolute path in local) and distinguishes the two by the leading slash, which is unambiguous because the folder name is validated against ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$.

    Two explicit consequences of the local mode:

    1. The Arquiteto's image gate (RN-105) does NOT apply. REVOKED by RN-494 (ADR 0135): the exemption ended — the three modes now require the image decision before opening the Code tab. The rest of this item is history. A Local project does not start a container, so the Code tab unlocked without waiting for a decision that was never going to happen. The exemption lived in the same funnel as the gate in the api, and the screen agreed: ProjectCodeTab did not even ask for the container state (RN-107) when the project was Local — if only the api exempted it, the tab would remain blocked on screen by a nonexistent decision.
    2. The permissions.json lives in the user's folder, together with the code — because the policy has to be read from the SAME root that the terminal scope authorizes.

    workspace_mode is not to be confused with the GitProviderName 'local': one says where the CODE lives on disk, the other where the git REPOSITORY lives, and the two choices are orthogonal.

    • Where: apps/api/src/db/schema/iam.ts (projects), apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.ts (projectScopeRoot), apps/api/src/domain/iam/project.entity.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/git/read-project-code.use-case.ts (portaoDoContainer), apps/web/src/routes/ProjectCodeTab.tsx, apps/engine/lib/engine/projects/project.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine/actions/workspace.ex (workspace_dir/2), apps/engine/lib/engine/dev/worktree_cleanup.ex (which was the second hand-written derivation, and started using the single one), apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.tsx
    • Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.spec.ts (describe "projectScopeRoot no modo local"), apps/api/test/infrastructure/filesystem/fs-permissions-file-store.spec.ts (the permissions.json in the user's folder), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/create-project-modo-de-workspace.spec.ts, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/git/read-project-code.use-case.spec.ts (a Local project does not go through the gate), apps/api/test/interfaces/http/iam/project-dto-modo-de-workspace.spec.ts (the mode is frozen: PATCH does not change it), apps/web/src/routes/ProjectCodeTab.test.tsx (the screen also exempts the gate), apps/engine/test/engine/actions/workspace_test.exs (describe "workspace_dir/2 com o localizador já resolvido"), apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.test.tsx

    RN-170 — A Local path is validated at CREATION, and the refusal teaches

    REVISED by RN-422 (ADR 0104): creation validation started to DIVERGE by mode — mounted (the renamed local) keeps touching the disk as described here, runner validates only the LEXICON, without I/O — the rest of this entry is history, faithful to what held until the revision.

    Creating a project in local mode with a path the api cannot reach produces a project that hangs later — on the first tool of the first agent, far from the screen where the decision was made. That is why creation refuses with 400, and the message says what needs to be done.

    The path must be:

    1. absolute, with no .. or . in any segment (the stored path is the path that is read; /srv/app/../../etc is /etc and does not look like it);
    2. existing and a folder inside the api container;
    3. writable by the process (access(W_OK|X_OK)) — the images run non-root (ADR 0024), and a host folder with another owner arrives mounted as read-only in practice;
    4. outside the root and the system folders (/, /etc, /usr, /var, /data… and everything below them): the project root is the scope that AUTHORIZES the agent's terminal (ADR 0055), and a project rooted at /etc turns "the agent writes in its project" into "the agent rewrites the container";
    5. with no overlap with the Brabo checkout, in BOTH directions — the folder that CONTAINS the monorepo and the folder INSIDE it. The second case is the problem that ADR 0055 reports actually happening.

    The stored path is the normalized one, not the raw string: validating one string and storing another is how validation stops holding the next day. A workspacePath sent together with workspace_mode: container is REFUSED, not ignored — a field silently discarded becomes "but I configured it".

    The LEXICAL part (items 1, 4 and 5) runs also on read, on each derivation of projectScopeRoot: the only way to bypass creation is to write directly into the database, and what is gained there is a terminal scope at /. The DISK part (items 2 and 3) runs only at creation, where the user can still fix it.

    The refusal for a missing folder brings the mount instruction — the file, the two services and the line (- <caminho>:<caminho>), with the pointer to the runbook. Mounting only in the api produces a project the api accepts and the engine does not see: it validates what it sees, and has no way of knowing what is mounted in the other container.

    • Where: apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.ts (validarCaminhoDeWorkspaceLocal, CaminhoLocalInvalidoError), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/create-project.use-case.ts (caminhoValidado), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/dto/create-project.dto.ts, apps/web/src/lib/wizard.ts (caminhoLocalParecePlausivel)
    • Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.spec.ts (describe "validarCaminhoDeWorkspaceLocal"), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/create-project-modo-de-workspace.spec.ts (describe "a criação RECUSA o caminho que travaria depois"), apps/web/src/lib/wizard.test.ts, apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.test.tsx
    • Architectural decision: ADR 0072
    • Origin: a guard required by the free-path variant (ADR 0072)

    RN-186 — provider é dimensão do relatório do owner, e só dele

    sumGroupedBy aceita provider como dimensão, e GET /workspaces/:id/spend-report devolve a lista porProvider ao lado de modelo, projeto, ator e dia. O ADR 0063 tinha deixado o eixo de fora; o ADR 0076 o devolveu sem revogar o argumento: quebrar gasto por provider continua sendo quebrar por CREDENCIAL, e por isso o eixo mora numa rota que já exige owner (RN-060) — a mesma régua de credential-spend, que segue respondendo a pergunta da FATURA (por mês, com o vínculo à chave que existe hoje).

    GET /projects/:id/spend/me não ganhou nada. A assimetria é o desenho: as duas respostas continuam não sendo recorte uma da outra (RN-101).

    A dimensão model não mudou: dois providers servindo o mesmo nome de modelo continuam numa linha só. Quem quer a quebra por credencial tem a lista própria, e cruzar as duas dimensões multiplicaria as linhas do ranking sem responder pergunta que as duas listas separadas já não respondam.

    RN-187 — A visão do membro não alcança provider, e quem garante é o TIPO

    Enquanto o eixo não existia, o que continha a visão do membro era a ausência de argumento a passar. Com o eixo de volta, a contenção passou a ser da assinatura: sumGroupedBy tem duas sobrecargas, e a que aceita um escopo com actor — o da audiência do membro, e o único que ele tem — só recebe SpendDimensionDoAtor, que é Exclude<SpendDimension, 'provider'>. sumGroupedBy('provider', escopoComAtor) não compila.

    Nem o repositório nem o caso de uso têm if sobre essa combinação, de propósito: uma checagem em tempo de execução daria a impressão de que a garantia é dinâmica, quando quem a sustenta é o compilador — e um if é o tipo de coisa que a próxima refatoração remove sem que nenhum teste fique vermelho.

    A barreira é dupla e as duas metades são independentes: a rota do membro também não tem parâmetro de dimensão (só projectId e dias), então uma query inventada como ?dimensao=provider é descartada pelo Nest antes de chegar ao handler.

    Exclude em vez de uma segunda lista escrita à mão é deliberado: dimensão nova nasce alcançável pelas duas audiências, e tirá-la do alcance do membro vira ato explícito neste ponto — nunca um esquecimento em outro arquivo.

    RN-188 — Pessoa e agente são partição da lista por ator, sem consulta a mais

    RN-189 — Embedding returns one vector per input, or an error

    embed is a BATCH operation: it receives N texts and returns N vectors, in the same order. Order is the only link between input and vector, and that's why a shorter response isn't usable — the i-th vector would end up belonging to another sentence, and the index would silently go wrong, with the symptom showing up in SEARCH, weeks later and far from the cause.

    So the contract refuses, rather than degrading, three things: an incomplete batch, an empty vector, and different dimensions in the same response. An empty input list is also refused before it goes out over the network — answering [] to it would make the caller record an empty index thinking it had indexed something.

    The result carries four fields, and each answers a question that already cost dearly somewhere else in the product: dimensions is checked against what CAME BACK (never copied from the catalog); model is what the provider said it used, because an alias resolves to a dated version and it's that name that goes to metering, for the same reason as the frozen price (RN-044); and inputTokens comes with estimated, preserving the "the provider said zero" × "the provider said nothing" distinction from RN-041.

    The error is thrown, normalized by code, instead of becoming a chunk like in chat. The chunk's reason is to preserve the spend of an in-progress turn; here there's nothing to preserve — either the provider returned the vectors and charged, or it didn't return them and didn't charge. It's the same choice as listModels, and the taxonomy is the same: no new LLMErrorCode.

    • Where: apps/api/src/application/ports/llm-provider.port.ts:61, apps/api/src/infrastructure/llm/embedding-result.ts:26
    • Test: test/contract/llm-provider.contract.ts (five cases, run against every provider that declares the capability)
    • Origin: ADR 0075

    RN-190 — Embedding has a capability in two layers, and the model's is exclusion

    As with tool calling (RN-040), the capability has two layers: the PROVIDER (capabilities.embeddings, the ceiling) and the MODEL (supportsEmbeddings on the catalog row). The difference between the two cases is exactly what the rule exists to state:

    • tool calling is a gradient — a model that doesn't request tools still converses, and that's why only the agent binding is refused;
    • embedding is exclusion — nomic-embed-text doesn't answer a question and llama3.2 doesn't return a vector. They're disjoint sets, and the Ollama daemon proves it by answering 501 ("This server does not support embeddings") to an embedding request with a chat model.

    assertCanEmbed checks both in the order that fails best: the provider first, because switching models doesn't fix a provider that doesn't embed. A model with no declaration is also refused, with a different message — absence means "the provider didn't say" (ADR 0041), never permission, and the right action for the reader is to sync the catalog rather than switch models. Deducing the capability from the model's NAME is forbidden: it would be a guess dressed up as data.

    • Where: apps/api/src/domain/llm/embedding-capability.ts:64, apps/api/src/infrastructure/llm/ollama-provider.ts:319
    • Test: test/domain/llm/embedding-capability.spec.ts, test/infrastructure/llm/ollama-provider.spec.ts
    • Origin: ADR 0075

    RN-191 — embeddings: true requires execution, not documentation

    The house rule (ADR 0041/ADR 0043) applied to the new capability: only ollama declares true, and the proof is POST /api/embed run against the real 0.32.1 daemon with nomic-embed-text — two inputs, two 768-dimension vectors, prompt_eval_count: 10.

    The other eight declare false, for two distinct reasons:

    • lack of proof (seven): there's no key for them in the environment, and the only paid smoke test that has ever run (acceptance) was for CHAT — in a hub, embedding routes to different providers than chat does, and proof of one endpoint isn't proof of the other;
    • operation absent (Anthropic): there's no dedicated embedding endpoint, and its docs point to a third party, which is a different provider with a different key and a different dialect.

    The OpenAI-compatible base's DIALECT is proven separately, with the contract suite running a second time over it with the capability turned on. That's what makes it cheap to flip a provider to true the day its key exists: it changes one line of the literal, and the parsing is already exercised. A provider that declares false and still exposes the method refuses the call before touching the network.

    RN-222 — The vector dimension is documented, not guessed, and embedding arrives after the chunk

    chunks.embedding is vector(768) — the real dimension of Ollama's nomic-embed-text, the only provider that today declares capabilities.embeddings: true (RN-191, ADR 0075). A vector index has a FIXED dimension: changing the embedding model in the future is a new migration, never a runtime parameter. The column is NULLABLE: this table stores the CHUNK (cut text), and the VECTOR may arrive later via an asynchronous indexing pipeline that does not exist yet (Onda 4) — without that, chunking would have to wait for embedding, mixing two failures of different nature (document parsing versus a network call to a provider) in a single atomic write.

    RN-223 — The vector index is HNSW, not IVFFlat, because the table is born empty

    IVFFlat needs rows already loaded to train the lists (lists) and performs poorly if built over an empty table — which is exactly the state of this table at birth, with no indexing pipeline yet (Onda 4). HNSW builds the graph incrementally, insertion by insertion, with no training step — good from the first row. vector_cosine_ops because it is the metric text embeddings generally expect (the similarity ranking should not change with the vector's magnitude).

    RN-225 — A migration that may require operator privilege is born in breaking/

Locally the role is a superuser, but nothing guarantees that in production — managed Postgres providers often do not give superuser to the application. If the migration fails there, it is an OPERATOR action before the deploy (running CREATE EXTENSION vector; once, as superuser), not a product bug — the CLAUDE.md criterion for being born in breaking/ instead of feature//bugfix/.

    RN-274 — Linking a social identity to an existing account requires an e-mail VERIFIED by the provider

A typed but unverified e-mail is not proof of identity: anyone can register someone else's e-mail at an OAuth provider. Accepting the link without that check would open account takeover — whoever already has alguem@empresa.com on Brabo didn't ask for someone else's GitHub, with that address only TYPED, to inherit the account. The refusal is 403, and no link is saved.

The guard if (process.argv[1]?.endsWith('analise-funil.ts')) void main(); at the end of the file is the same as medir-execucao.ts: without it, importing the module in the test would bring up all of Nest and take down the process at the argument parser's process.exit.

    RN-321 — The funnel counts SESSIONS per stage, only executed actions, and lead time uses the execution's updated_at

    calcularFunil counts how many sessions produced at least one git_commit, pr_open, and git_merge with status: 'executed' — a session with three commits enters only once in each stage it reached, never three times. A stage's conversion rate is sessions-of-the-stage / sessions-of-the-previous-stage, and is null (not 0, not Infinity) when the denominator is zero — there's no "conversion from" anything to measure. calcularLeadTimes uses the updated_at of the proposed_actions row, not created_at: it's the instant when ExecuteGitActionUseCase#record actually wrote the execution_result (updateExecutionResult bumps updatedAt), not when the action was PROPOSED — the same distinction that token_usage/frozen price already make in another context (RN-042). A merge whose updated_at precedes the commit's (two batches in the same session, or incoherent data) is discarded, never becoming a negative lead time.

    The implementavel gate activates — QA-strategy as the qa-lead's second moment (RN-340/341, ADR 0090)

    RN-340 — The implementavel gate decides the story BEFORE the dev agent writes code

    docs/gates.yml declared the implementavel gate (owner dev-lead) since PHASE 14d with status: planned — never activated. ADR 0090 activates it: the Dev Lead's assess_implementability tool proposes the implementability opinion of a story (implementavel/inviavel + justification) as a proposed_action, the SAME pattern as propose_execution_plan (RN-284) — three outcomes ({:ok, texto} | {:pending, action_id} | {:error, texto}), minimum role maintainer in decide.ts, and DELIBERATELY outside the block of absolute ceilings (it's an initial decision, not exceeding a ceiling).

    The opinion depends on the test plan, which is a PREREQUISITE, not an argument. run_assessment/2 reads the story's most recent artifact.plano_de_teste in the HISTORY of the Dev Lead's own session (emitted by the QA-strategy, RN-341):

    1. No plan yet — triggers Engine.Gates.Dispatcher.run_qa_estrategia/3 (the same test-swappable indirection that run_qa/2/run_secops/2 already use) and returns {:error, texto} asking to try again shortly. A tool error is an INPUT to the loop, not the end of the line (RN-163): the Dev Lead has a ceiling of 14 iterations to try again. The wait window is accepted and declared — QA-strategy runs in a separate process (qa-lead), and a synchronous run/2 can't block waiting for the result without coupling the two processes.
    2. With a plan — builds the opinion with the test plan EMBEDDED in the payload (synthesis and executable criteria), so the user can decide without needing to open two events, and proposes the action.

    Since RN-674 (ADR 0192) the two steps above NO LONGER hold. The test plan is born AFTER the dev's delivery and feeds qa-verificada; run_assessment/2 neither reads nor triggers a plan, proposes the opinion on the FIRST call, over the story and the module_map the Dev Lead already has in context, and the payload lost planoDeTeste/criteriosExecutaveis. Dispatcher.run_qa_estrategia/3 was removed. The rest of this rule (proposal, three outcomes, minimum role, outside the absolute ceilings) remains the same.

    secops-runtime — abuse report over rate_limit_hits (RN-375..377, ADR 0091)

    A conscious decision by the product owner to bring forward the secops-runtime role (docs/fluxo.yml, camada_seguranca), which was born proposto with the separation criterion "production with real traffic (after DEPLOY_ENABLED + platform active)". That trigger didn't fire — there's no production traffic. What exists today is rate_limit_hits (RateLimitGuard, ADR 0027): one row per counted request, written even under dev/CI traffic. secops-runtime comes in as a SCRIPT (pnpm --filter api relatorio:seguranca-runtime), not an LLM agent nor a GenServer — there's no decision to make, only data to aggregate.

    RN-375 — The report declares the window, never pretends a longer history

    DomainGaugesCollector.pruneRateLimit (apps/api/src/infrastructure/observability/domain-gauges.collector.ts:177-186) deletes hits older than 2 × RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS (240s with the default of 60s), every METRICS_GAUGE_INTERVAL_MS (15s by default) — the table never keeps more than a few minutes. relatorio-seguranca-runtime.ts prints TWO windows, never just one: the CONFIGURED one (the pruning's theoretical ceiling) and the OBSERVED one (what the data actually covers, from the first to the last occurred_at read). When the two coincide, the report says explicitly that it's a sign of pruning — older hits may have existed and have already been deleted — never "there were no more hits than that".

    RN-376 — The ranking works only with what bucket_key keeps: bucket and when

    RateLimitGuard.registrarEContar (apps/api/src/interfaces/http/shared/rate-limit.guard.ts:150-170) records only bucket_key (user:<uuid> or ip:<endereço>) and occurred_at — there's NO route, HTTP method, nor block reason. rankingDeBaldes and interpretarBalde (apps/api/scripts/relatorio-seguranca-runtime.ts) classify by these two fields and only them; a bucket_key outside the user:/ip: format falls into desconhecido instead of blowing up, so the script doesn't break if a future RateLimitGuard writes another format. Asking for an "IP ranking by route" would be inventing a dimension the table never kept.

    The dbre role becomes two mechanical scripts (RN-400..403, ADR 0093)

    RN-400 — The migration opinion is STATIC SQL analysis, and ignores the risk pattern when it appears only in a comment

    lintarConteudo (the pure core of lint-migracao.ts) scans each .sql of apps/api/src/db/migrations/ line by line, without depending on --projeto or a database — the risk it finds is SCHEMA risk, not load risk, and that's why it doesn't depend on any real data volume (the separation criterion that docs/fluxo.yml already declared for the role). Five patterns, each with the reason attached to the finding: DROP TABLE/TRUNCATE (total loss, irreversible), DROP COLUMN (loss of the column, irreversible), ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE/SET DATA TYPE (can rewrite the whole table), and ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL without DEFAULT (fails against a non-empty table — the pattern 0042_tough_captain_midlands.sql consciously avoided, with nullable-first-then-backfill-then-SET NOT NULL).

    A line starting with -- (comment) is ignored on purpose: this repository explains in prose, in the SQL itself, why a pattern was AVOIDED — analyzing the comment's text would find the pattern exactly in the sentence describing why it wasn't used.

    • Where: apps/api/scripts/lint-migracao.ts (REGRAS, line 75; lintarConteudo, line 126)
    • Test: apps/api/test/scripts/lint-migracao.spec.ts — each pattern individually, a combination of several in the same migration, and "ignora o padrão de risco quando ele aparece só em COMENTÁRIO"

    fluxo.yml × code audit — Wave 6 (last): the necessidade-validada gate (RN-406, ADR 0095)

    RN-408 — MAIL_TRANSPORT=smtp gates boot by the RN-114 pattern, without the public default

    Closes the backlog item "Real SMTP in MailSender" (ADR 0096). resolverConfigSmtp() validates SMTP_HOST/SMTP_USER/SMTP_PASSWORD/ SMTP_FROM in the SAME format as RN-114 — in production (NODE_ENV === 'production'), each one takes down the boot if missing, whitespace only, or (in the case of SMTP_HOST) equal to the example literal published (commented out) in .env.example. SMTP_FROM has one more check: it must match "Nome <email@dominio>" or just email@dominio. An invalid SMTP_PORT (non-numeric or outside 1–65535) also takes down the boot in production.

    The difference from the original RN-114 is structural, not of rigor: the four secrets of RN-114 (AUTH_JWT_SECRET and company) HAVE a public development default, and it's the existence of that default that makes "not empty" an insufficient check. Here there's no default at all — SMTP_HOST stays blank if nobody sets it —, so the whole ruler is only applied when NODE_ENV=production AND MAIL_TRANSPORT=smtp. Outside production, or with the transport at log (the default, including in production), none of the five variables is required: sending real e-mail is opt-in by the operator, and without that explicit opt-in the behavior stays the usual log-only one — including in production, so that whoever already runs the product today doesn't break on updating.

    The validation runs inside the constructor of SmtpMailSender, exercised by the useFactory of AuthUseCasesModule when assembling Nest's provider graph (NestFactory.create()) — not by an eager call in main.ts, like the four secrets of the original RN-114. The difference is deliberate: those four protect a path that ANY request can exercise at any moment, so failing before coming up matters. SmtpMailSender is only instantiated when the operator opted for smtp, and AuthUseCasesModule is imported unconditionally (via AuthHttpModule), so validation still happens at boot — the same design CREDENTIALS_MASTER_KEY already uses (validated in the constructor of EnvelopeEncryptionService, exercised by the same graph assembly).

    • Where: apps/api/src/infrastructure/mail/smtp-config.ts (resolverConfigSmtp, resolverModoDeTransporte), apps/api/src/infrastructure/mail/smtp-mail-sender.ts (SmtpMailSender, calls resolverConfigSmtp() in the constructor), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/auth-use-cases.module.ts (useFactory of the MailSender)
    • Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/mail/smtp-config.spec.ts (same pattern as auth-key-material.spec.ts/service-token.spec.ts), apps/api/test/infrastructure/mail/smtp-mail-sender.spec.ts
    • Origin: ADR 0096, extending the pattern of RN-114 (which in turn extends ADR 0059)

    Automatic personal workspace on sign-up (RN-410)

    Found while navigating the product after a database reset: the dashboard's "New project"/"+" button did NOTHING, with no error at all. The root cause was in two layers. The visible one: Dashboard.tsx only opens the NewProjectWizard when useCurrentWorkspace() finds a workspace (list[0]?.workspace from GET /workspaces); with none, the click has nowhere to go. The deep one: RegisterUseCase created user and credential but NEVER a workspace, and the same held for SocialLoginCallbackUseCase in the branch that provisions a new account — EVERY new sign-up, by password or by social login, hit that wall. It just hadn't shown up before because db/seed.ts always creates a workspace along with the demo data, and no product screen calls createWorkspace (the route, the use case, and the HTTP client exist — they just have no caller at all in the UI).

    RN-410 — Every NEW account is born with a personal workspace, in the SAME transaction as the account

    RegisterUseCase (e-mail/password registration) and SocialLoginCallbackUseCase (provisioning a new account via social login) create the workspace and add the user as owner — the same create/addMember pair that CreateWorkspaceUseCase already uses — inside the SAME transaction that already creates user and credential. It isn't a second call to the use case: that one opens its OWN transaction, and the point is that a user without a workspace never exists if something fails midway.

    RN-412 — dev.awaiting_gate/dev.awaiting_approval hold the session; the effective compaction window is consistent with the transport

    Found by real USE ("on PRs it's always blowing up with entity too large"), with two defects that chain together. The QA/SecOps gate died with 413 request entity too large → the dev agent waiting for the verdict stayed stuck in dev.awaiting_gate indefinitely → that state was NOT one of the three RN-411 held → the 30s heartbeat closed the session from underneath → the Executors tab required an active session (findActiveExecutionSession) and erased the entire roster, even with real work hanging.

    The cause of the 413 was Brabo's own api, never the LLM provider — see ADR 0098. Two fixes, both necessary (one without the other only postpones the overflow):

    1. apps/api/src/main.ts never configured Express's body limit — the 100 KB default applied, the narrowest bottleneck in the engine→api direction (Phoenix accepts up to 8 MB). POST /internal/sessions/:sessionId/llm-turn resends the conversation's ENTIRE history on each ToolLoop iteration, and 3-4 tool results of 32 KiB (RN-150's individual ceiling) already added up to more than 100 KB. API_JSON_BODY_LIMIT (default 10mb) closes that end.
    2. Engine.Harness.ContextManager.Default had two defects that made compaction unreachable before the body overflowed: estimate/1 counted only content, so assistant messages with heavy toolCalls cost ~zero tokens in the estimate; and the compaction window used only context_window (128,000 tokens in the gate agents — qa_automacao_agent.ex, qa_performance_seguranca_agent.ex, qa_estrategia_agent.ex, appsec_agent.ex, dev_agent_server.ex), giving ~350 KB before compacting (threshold 0.7 × window). The EFFECTIVE window is now min(context_window, transport_ceiling) (transport_max_body_bytes, a single config, default 8 MiB), and the cut always happens at an ITERATION BOUNDARY of the ToolLoop (group_by_iteration/1) — never separating an assistant message with toolCalls from the role: "tool" that answer it, which would break the provider's tool-use protocol.

    The pending-work ruler (DEV_PENDING_TYPES, get-session-pending-work.use-case.ts) gained two types: dev.awaiting_gate (the original argument — the gate now shouldn't die anymore, but locking the session because of it was never correct, it's defense in depth) and dev.awaiting_approval, by an argument DIFFERENT from what RN-411 had discarded: the approval/denial decision writes proposed_actions.status SYNCHRONOUSLY in the ApproveActionUseCase transaction (the second signal no longer sees pending there), but the dev agent's resumption is ASYNCHRONOUS — only after avisarQuemEsperava() writes task.action_settled/task.pr_settled to the outbox does Engine.Outbox.Drain enqueue the Oban job that wakes DevAgentServer. In that window, nothing held the session: the same defect as RN-411, one level deeper.

    The Executors/Overview tabs had the sibling defect on the web side: executionActivated was derived from events.some((e) => e.type === 'execution.activated') over the window of only 200 events of useSessionEvents ({ limit: 200, latest: true }) — execution.activated is among the FIRST events of an execution session and left the window in any real session. The correct value already existed, aggregated over ALL events (bool_or(...), RN-090), in the workspace summary (ProjectCardSummary.roster.executionActivated) — ProjectExecutorsTab.tsx and ProjectOverviewTab.tsx now consume it instead of deriving from the window. gatesEverOpened suffers from the SAME class of defect and was DECLARED as a known limitation, not fixed here — fixing it would require changing the signature of deriveAgentRoster/rosterFactsFromEvents, outside the scope of this fix.

    • Where: apps/api/src/main.ts, apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/context_manager.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tokenizer.ex, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/sessions/get-session-pending-work.use-case.ts, apps/web/src/routes/ProjectExecutorsTab.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/ProjectOverviewTab.tsx
    • Test: apps/api/test/main.spec.ts (1 MB body accepted; above the limit → 413); apps/engine/test/engine/harness/context_manager_test.exs (heavy toolCalls trigger compaction; :pinned survives; the transport ceiling forces compaction even with a large model window); get-session-pending-work.use-case.spec.ts (last event dev.awaiting_gate/dev.awaiting_approval → pending: true); ProjectExecutorsTab.test.tsx/ProjectOverviewTab.test.tsx (a session with >200 events still shows the roster via the aggregated summary)

    RN-416 — The graph is DERIVED memory, rebuildable by projection from the outbox

    The alternative of the engine writing to Neo4j directly was REFUSED — it would open a second write path besides the event log, breaking the guarantee of a single source of truth. GraphProjector (api) drains a SECOND outbox row, the usual same transaction, aggregateType: 'graph_projection' — a value the engine-side Engine.Outbox.Drain never matches (its filter is aggregate_type IN ('session', 'task')), avoiding the race that would exist if it reused 'session' (the engine already drains and marks that type in ~2s). Same pattern as deny-action.use-case.ts, which already writes in two aggregateTypes in the same transaction.

    Instrumented at two points: AppendSessionEventUseCase (for handoff.offered, psychologist.hypothesis_proposed, anamnese.profile_updated — payload only {eventId}, the projector REREADS the complete envelope from the event log at projection time, never trusting a potentially stale copy) and TransitionSessionUseCase (for session.closed/session.closed_abnormally, which don't go through session_events). GraphProjector is a poller (~2s, same shape as DomainGaugesCollector) that calls the write use cases already existing from the previous foundation — idempotency lives IN THEM (natural key per type: Hipotese.id, Handoff(sessionId,seq), PerfilAnamnese(userId,dimensao), Interacao.sessionId with range extension). A GraphUnavailableError in the middle of a batch STOPS the whole cycle (the rest would fail for the same reason) — the row stays unprocessed and retries on its own in the next cycle, with no intervention.

    • Test: graph-projector.spec.ts (happy path of the four types; evidence→seq resolution of a hypothesis; GraphUnavailableError leaves the row unmarked and stops the cycle; the following cycle reprocesses successfully; reprocessing the SAME row twice doesn't duplicate in the graph); new tests in append-session-event.use-case.spec.ts/ transition-session.use-case.spec.ts (a projectable type writes the second row; a non-projectable type writes nothing extra)

    RN-424 — A PAT authenticates ONLY runner-ticket, by construction — never dual-auth with JWT on that route

    A Personal Access Token (brb_…) never authorizes any route other than POST /projects/:projectId/runner-ticket. The guarantee isn't an if that a new route could forget to check: it's structural. @RequirePatAuth() marks the handler with IS_PAT_ROUTE_KEY; JwtAuthGuard (the global APP_GUARD) checks that metadata BEFORE trying JWT verify() and returns true without validating anything — the same bypass shape that IS_PUBLIC_KEY and IS_SERVICE_ROUTE_KEY already use. PatAuthGuard, applied only to that handler via @UseGuards(), is what actually authenticates: it extracts the bearer, refuses (401) any value not starting with brb_ without querying the repository — it never tries to validate as JWT on that route, and no other route accepts brb_… as a bearer.

    After PatAuthGuard populates request.user, RolesGuard/ ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase keep running, unchanged — belt and suspenders: if the PAT's owner loses sufficient role in the project through the normal path (ProjectMember/workspace), the token stops authorizing even without having been explicitly revoked.

    The alternative considered and refused: the global JwtAuthGuard recognizing the brb_ prefix and populating request.user directly, for ANY route. That would authorize the PAT for everything the user's role allows in the rest of the api — the "only asks for a runner ticket" scope would become decorative.

    RN-425 — PAT validation collapses nonexistent/revoked/expired into a single answer; wrong scope is 403; last_used_at is never throttled

    PersonalAccessTokenRepository.validarEUsar(hash) is ONE query: UPDATE personal_access_tokens SET last_used_at = now() WHERE token_hash = $1 AND revoked_at IS NULL AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now()) RETURNING id, user_id, project_id. Zero rows returns null, and the guard answers 401 for "doesn't exist", "revoked", and "expired" with the SAME message — whoever presents a stolen or expired token doesn't find out which of the three is the reason (same pattern as AccountTokenRepository.consumir()).

    Incorrect project scope is a DIFFERENT category: if the project_id returned by the query doesn't match the route's :projectId, it's 403, not 401 — the token really authenticated, it just has no right to THIS project.

    last_used_at is updated UNCONDITIONALLY, in the SAME validation query — never with a throttle (e.g. "only if last_used_at is NULL or older than 5 minutes") in the same WHERE. A throttle there is a real bug: a PAT presented twice in under 5 minutes would fall out of the WHERE the second time (because last_used_at would be "too fresh"), and the query would return zero rows for a valid token — rejecting a legitimate reconnection with 401. The runner's retry loop reconnects in seconds, not minutes. The cost of not throttling is a one-row UPDATE by unique index per call — irrelevant in the real worst case (up to 10 attempts in a row, the runner's ceiling).

    • Where: apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/personal-access-token.repository.ts (validarEUsar), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/auth/pat-auth.guard.ts

Each user only sees and only revokes their OWN tokens — including within a project where they're maintainer.

    RN-439 — POST .../runner-ticket authenticates AND authorizes in the SAME guard; RolesGuard (global) abstains on an @RequirePatAuth() route

    POST /projects/:projectId/runner-ticket answered 403 "Não autenticado" for EVERY PAT, even a valid one, freshly issued, scoped to the right project — found in a LIVE verification of brabo-runner connecting to a real project, never by an automated test. Root cause: JwtAuthGuard and RolesGuard are the two APP_GUARDs — GLOBAL — and a global guard ALWAYS runs BEFORE a route's LOCAL guard (@UseGuards), regardless of the order of the decorators in the controller. JwtAuthGuard already knew how to abstain on this route (the IS_PAT_ROUTE_KEY bypass already existed, without populating request.user, counting on PatAuthGuard to authenticate afterwards); RolesGuard didn't, and refused every call with request.user still empty — PatAuthGuard never got to run. The controller's comment described the order backwards ("RolesGuard runs AFTER PatAuthGuard"), and it never was so.

    The fix followed the SAME pattern JwtAuthGuard already used for this problem: RolesGuard gained the twin bypass (IS_PAT_ROUTE_KEY → returns true without checking request.user), delegating the entire authorization to whoever becomes the ONLY guard running after request.user is populated on this route — PatAuthGuard itself, which now also reads @RequireRole (via Reflector) and resolves the effective role (ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase.forProject), refusing with the SAME message RolesGuard would use ("Papel insuficiente para esta ação"). The logic is duplicated between the two guards ON PURPOSE — RolesGuard lives in iam, PatAuthGuard lives in auth, and a cross dependency just to reuse ~10 lines wouldn't be worth it.

    A SECOND defect was hidden behind the first, and only showed up when the integration test started exercising the two guards TOGETHER: PatAuthGuard compared the RAW token directly against personal_access_tokens.token_hash in validarEUsar — which always expects the HASH (hashDeToken, HMAC-SHA256+ pepper, the same one TokenFactory/IssuePersonalAccessTokenUseCase use to write). Fixed to this.tokens.validarEUsar(hashDeToken(token)). While RolesGuard refused everything before, this second bug never got to manifest — fixing only the first would have swapped an always-403 for an always-401, and the runner would still never really connect.

    Revised by RN-687 (ADR 0203, 10/01): the browser flow was RETIRED, and POST .../runner-device-keys left with it — together with RegisterRunnerDeviceKeyUseCase and its test, cited below as they were. The project keys already registered remain valid and revocable.

POST/DELETE .../runner-device-keys require the minimum role developer and are authenticated by the normal SESSION JWT (unlike runner-ticket: whoever calls here is the already logged-in browser registering its own device, not the runner running without a session). RegisterRunnerDeviceKeyUseCase validates only the minimal SHAPE of the JWK (kty:"OKP", crv:"Ed25519", x present) — the deep validation (whether it's really a valid Ed25519 point) is left to jose.importJWK at the moment of use, in RN-465. RevokeRunnerDeviceKeyUseCase is IDEMPOTENT and scoped to the calling userId — the same design as revogar() of RN-426 — and returns 404 both for a nonexistent key and for another user's key, the same discipline of not leaking existence.

    Declared asymmetry with the PAT: unlike RN-427 (a maintainer revokes the PAT of ANY user of the project, incident response), the device key does NOT have an equivalent maintainer route today — only self-revocation. The docblock of RunnerDeviceKeysController declares this explicitly as a cut of this round, not forgetfulness: extending the same pattern of RN-427 to device keys is direct future work, if it comes to be requested.

    • Origin: product owner's request

    RN-465 — POST .../runner-ticket accepts a PAT OR a device key (Ed25519, TTL ≤60s) — a second form of DEVICE credential, never dual-auth with the session JWT (RN-439's distinction)

    Revised by RN-687 (ADR 0203, 10/01): nothing of this RN changed in the guard — PatAuthGuard still accepts the JWT of a PROJECT key, and that's why a runner configured through the browser before ADR 0203 doesn't break. What no longer exists is creating a NEW project key: the browser no longer generates the pair.

    PatAuthGuard gained a second path, next to the unchanged PAT (brb_...): a bearer in compact JWT format (three segments) is treated as a device key. The guard reads the header's kid (without verifying the signature yet), fetches the corresponding ACTIVE public key in runner_device_keys, and only then verifies the EdDSA signature with jose.importJWK/jwtVerify. Short and MANDATORY TTL: exp - iat can't exceed 60s — checked against the token's SIGNED life, not against "now", closing the replay window of a leaked JWT from the moment it was signed. The userId/projectId used to authorize always come from the record saved in the database, never from a JWT claim — the token only needs to prove possession of the private key, never to state who the owner is. projectId is checked TWICE (the JWT's claim against the route, and the key's registered project against the route) — the same 401 vs 403 discipline the PAT path already uses: a token/key valid for the WRONG project is a different category from an invalid token/key. The runner signs that JWT in assinarTicketComChaveDeDispositivo (apps/runner/src/auth.ts), with the private JWK already LOADED in memory — never reading a file there, preserving the "no file I/O" guarantee of auth.ts (whoever reads the file is RN-466's separate module).

    This does NOT reopen RN-439: RN-439 closed the guarantee that runner-ticket never accepts the LOGIN JWT as a credential — it still stands. The device key is a DIFFERENT JWT, self-signed by the runner itself with a key whose private part the api never saw, with no user sub at all — only a second way of proving "I am the device of such user in this project", as scoped as the PAT it complements. Accepting the session JWT here would make RolesGuard/@RequireRole authorize that user for everything their role allows in the rest of the api, blowing past the runner:project:<id> scope — exactly what RN-439 prevented.

    The two downgrade ceilings in project_members (RN-472)

    RN-472 — Nobody downgrades the workspace owner, and nobody downgrades themselves

    RN-471 recorded that ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase.forProject is projectRole ?? workspaceRole — the project row OVERRIDES the workspace one, in both directions. What it didn't keep is the consequence: AddProjectMemberUseCase was a one-line passthrough to the upsert, and neither of the two write paths looked at WHO the target is. Any maintainer could (a) downgrade the workspace owner to viewer in a project, taking the owner out of their own project, and (b) downgrade themselves with no way to undo it, because undoing is the same route, which requires maintainer.

    The override STAYS in both directions. forProject doesn't change. Restricting someone in a sensitive project (workspace developer → viewer in project X) is a deliberate capability, and "the higher of the two" would eliminate it — the resolve-effective-role.use-case.spec.ts fixes the upward half since Phase 1. What comes in are TWO ceilings, and only them:

    ceiling what it refuses status
    1 a role below owner for whoever is the WORKSPACE owner 403
    2 a role below what the CALLER has today, when the target is themselves 403

    The owner is workspace_members.role, never workspaces.created_by. Both exist in db/schema/iam.ts and they're not the same thing: created_by is a historical fact, and it's the role that authorization uses in all the rest of the system (forWorkspace is workspaces.findMemberRole; created_by doesn't appear in any authorization path). Reading created_by would shield the creator who has already transferred ownership and leave uncovered the current owner who created nothing — the hole the ceiling exists to close.

    Ceiling 2 is "themselves", with no threshold — not "below maintainer". The version with a threshold would copy a number from the controller's @RequireRole into the domain and would age silently if the route changed its minimum. The price, declared: the owner who wanted to set themselves as maintainer in their own project (a reversible move) is also refused, and now needs another maintainer. Raising one's own role isn't a downgrade and still passes.

    The ceilings live in the USE CASE, with the rule in the domain — not in RolesGuard. The guard authorizes the CALLER against the route's @RequireRole and doesn't see the body (dto.role) nor the target (dto.userId); the two ceilings are about the TARGET and about the actor↔target relation. The SHAPE is that of domain/actions/decide.ts (RN-154/RN-418): a pure function, the message next to the condition, with no configuration key. What doesn't carry over is the outcome — there the ceiling becomes require_approval over an agent's proposed_action, here the call is already human and synchronous and there's no queue to send it to.

    403, not 409 nor 400: it's an authorization refusal — the caller has the route's role and doesn't have authority for this move. Waiting changes nothing (it isn't a state conflict) and the body is valid (the same body with another target would pass).

    What the ceilings do NOT cover, and remains possible: downgrading another maintainer who isn't a workspace owner; self-downgrade through REMOVAL — RemoveProjectMemberUseCase got no ceiling, and removing one's own row drops the effective role to the workspace role, which is benign when the workspace holds it and irreversible when it doesn't (maintainer only through the project row, viewer in the workspace); self-PROMOTION, which was already possible before; and downgrading the owner IN THE WORKSPACE (POST workspaces/:workspaceId/members still has no ceiling). The two removal cases are FIXED in tests, including the open one.

    The screen is left for later, and the refusal shows up. MembersSection computes ceiling 2 on its own, but not ceiling 1: listProjectMembers returns the role of the PROJECT ROW, and the target's workspace role isn't within the client's reach. Half a gate would be a Select honest about one refusal and silent about the other — the second source of role RN-471 writes against. Meanwhile, handleRoleChange already shows mensagemDaApi(erro, …) in a toast (RN-471), and it's the api's sentence that says which ceiling was hit.

    The kid is the link, and the refusal has a name (RN-475)

    RN-477 — Provisioning that fails SAYS it failed, and the wait for it has a ceiling

    Repository provisioning runs entirely inside the POST — there's no worker nor queue behind it (the OpenAPI description that promised "continues in the background" was wrong and was fixed). A failure, therefore, has already happened when the response arrives. This RN is about the screen never asserting "provisioning" about work that has already ended badly.

    Every failure becomes a DURABLE state, and there were two paths that didn't. The first is step.check(), which was outside every try/catch in the BootstrapRunner and does network IO: a 401 from an expired token, a 403, or a timeout went up without touching the row, which stayed pending with lastError: NULL. The second is the refusal in createRepo, which happens before the row exists — repo_bootstraps is only born after the provider confirms the repository, so the project was left with ZERO rows. Now the first writes status: 'failed' + lastError in a single place (the step's catch) and emits bootstrap.step_failed; and the second is read by the status endpoint from the failed git_repo_create proposed_action.

    The creation failure does NOT invent a step. failedStep stays null: the repository never came to exist, so none of the six Gitflow steps was attempted, and naming one to fill in the sentence would be swapping a silence for wrong information. The screen has its own title for that case, without {{step}}.

    The screen shows the reason and offers a way out. The empty-bodied .catch(() => {}) of ProvisioningPage — whose comment asserted that "the failure appears via bootstrapQuery", which was false on both paths above — now keeps the api's message and displays it. The "Try again" button no longer depends on status === 'provision_failed': it also appears when the POST refused, which is precisely when there's no failure status to depend on.

    The wait has a CEILING and three states that don't collapse, exactly like RN-474 and for the same reason: the 1s poll was infinite. After 3 minutes without converging, the screen says it stopped following, declares that this doesn't prove failure (provisioning runs inside the request, and a slow provider may still be working) and offers "look again" — which rearms the wait without triggering a second POST, because a second POST would create one more bootstrap session.

    The dashboard card knows. The read model queries the failed git_repo_create actions together with the bootstrap rows, so a project that failed before a cursor existed no longer appears without any badge — and the click once again leads to the provisioning screen, which only redirected on provision_failed.

    • Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/git/provision-repository.use-case.spec.ts (a failure in CHECK becomes failed with reason and event; a failure to CREATE leaves no row but the status reports it, with null failedStep), apps/api/test/domain/git/repo-bootstrap-status.spec.ts (no row with a creation failure; with a row the old failure is ignored; pure pending), apps/web/src/routes/ProvisioningPage.test.tsx (the reason appears; the retry exists without provision_failed; the wait stops and says what it doesn't know; a title without a step doesn't invent one)
