    RN-581 — The conversation in progress holds the session for up to 8h, and the closed session refuses conversation

    In exp001 the heartbeat closed the session 30 seconds after the tab stopped, with the Criativo having just asked — and the event log kept receiving events for four minutes after closed_at. Two defects, one on each side of the closing: none of the pending-work signals of RN-064 saw a conversation waiting for the user (a Criativo that finished its turn is idle, without a handoff, without an action, without dev.*), and nothing — neither the events funnel, nor the conversation use cases, nor the engine — looked at the session's state before writing.

    The rule, on the heartbeat side:

    1. A conversation waiting for the user is pending work. It is the FIFTH signal of pending-work: the session's most recent end-of-turn event (agent.response, chat.structured_question or agent.error on the agent's side; chat.message or chat.structured_question_answered on the user's side) is the AGENT's, and the actor is a conversational one. agent.error counts as end of turn on purpose: by RN-059 the agent says in the thread what happened, and the next move is the user's. Speech from someone who does not converse (Psicólogo, dev agent) does not hold.
    2. It is the only signal with a CEILING: 8 hours, counted from the END of the agent's turn (the created_at of that event), not from the last heartbeat. The api returns the instant (aguardandoUsuarioDesde) and the engine applies the ceiling (SESSION_CONVERSATION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, default 28800000). Past it, the session closes closed with its OWN cause, conversation_idle_timeout — not heartbeat_timeout, because whoever reads termination_reason (the Psicólogo, a per-session metric) needs to separate the tab that vanished from the conversation nobody resumed. The TerminationClassifier reads it as :timeout: the api knows six causes in the hypotheses, and opening a seventh would be changing that contract. The ceiling also holds with the tab OPEN (AT-152): the SessionServer has its own clock (:conversation_idle_check, every 5 min — no environment variable, only the test hook :session_conversation_idle_check_ms), independent of the heartbeat — the tab's ping neither resets nor postpones it. On each round it reads the pending item and only CLOSES by ceiling (same cause, conversation_idle_timeout); api down, no pending item or a pending item without an instant only reschedule, because what closes due to api down is still the heartbeat. Before, the ceiling was only checked when the heartbeat expired, and an open tab (ping every ~10s) made it unreachable: an immortal session.
    3. A signal without a ceiling wins. With an offered handoff, a pending action, an agent in a turn or a dev agent working, the instant comes back null and the session stays without a ceiling, as it always did. That is why the signal is the LAST in the list.
    4. A present and unreadable instant is an ERROR, never nil. nil with pending: true is a pending item without a ceiling; a broken format would become an immortal session. As an error, it falls into the api-down path — it closes by heartbeat, saying why.

    The rule, on the closed session side:

    1. A closed/closed_abnormally session refuses a CONVERSATION event with a NAMED 409: { message, reason: "sessao_encerrada", status, type }. closing still accepts — the lock is on TERMINAL state.
    2. "Conversation" has two clauses, and both are necessary. The TYPE only exists as conversation (chat.message, chat.structured_question[_answered], agent.status, agent.activated, handoff.offered/accepted, readiness.confirmed, necessity.validated, architecture.readiness_confirmed), OR the ACTOR is a conversational agent (the six plus dev-lead and infra). An ALLOWLIST by type was measured and refused: those who legitimately write to a closed session are the CONSUMERS of the closing — the Psicólogo runs a ToolLoop against it and writes tool.call, agent.response, agent.error; the Anamnese writes its own outcomes —, and they speak the SAME generic vocabulary as the Criativo. The type is the same; who differs is the actor.
    3. The human decision about an action keeps coming in. action.approved/ action.denied and the execution outcomes are not conversation: the action is an item of a DURABLE queue that survives the session, and refusing the decision would leave a pending item impossible to resolve. The normal case does not even get here (a pending action holds the session, signal 2 of RN-064); it only exists when the session died through another door.
    4. The refusal leaves no trace. The state comes from the SAME UPDATE that reserves the seq (with no extra query on the hottest path, under the same row lock as the transition), and the refusal throws inside the transaction: the increment comes back, the seq stays without a hole. The human chat, which writes chat.message without the funnel, has the same lock. The use cases with an effect BEFORE the event refuse before the effect: CreateHandoff before creating the row, AcceptHandoff before marking accepted (which would activate the next agent), ActivateAgent before calling the engine.
    5. The closing STOPS the conversational agents. SessionLifecycleWorker, through which every closing goes (heartbeat, idle conversation, human, crash), stops the session's conversational agents on ALL nodes (Engine.Agents.Conversacionais, via :erpc — the registry is local and the job lands on any replica). The turn in progress is ABANDONED in the terminate/2 of the six servers (TurnoAssincrono.abandonar/1): the task dies without writing or broadcasting anything, because writing would be asking the api for what it refuses. There is no answer to give: since RN-578 (ADR 0163) whoever triggered the turn already received :ok on acceptance. For the same reason the offer_dev_handoff the Arquiteto kept for the turn's closing does NOT run when the closing is the session's — the handoff would be refused (since RN-672 there is nothing to keep anymore: the handoff to the Dev Lead comes from the Infra). The Infra Lead, which runs the turn inside handle_call, is killed if it does not exit within 5s.
    6. The refusal is never silent in the engine. Almost every caller of append_event/3 discards the return; the client logs the 409 sessao_encerrada as a warning, and the return stays the same.
    7. The screen recognizes the 409 by the CODE and says the session closed (AT-154). ehRecusaDeSessaoEncerrada checks status === 409 AND body.reason === "sessao_encerrada" — never the text, and never only the 409, which is also "turn in progress". In the four conversation actions (send a message, answer a structured question, confirm the readiness of the Criativo and of the Arquiteto) the screen shows its own sentence instead of the generic error, redoes the session read (it is the new status that makes the composer disappear) and does NOT lose what was typed: the message goes back to the draft and shows up read-only in place of the composer, and the form's answers stay in the fields. The sentence does not promise "Reopen" — the action does not exist. And the "Close" button stays inert in BOTH terminal states (sessaoEhTerminal, the mirror of isTerminal), not only in closed (AT-155).

    What this rule does NOT close: the ceiling is only checked when the HEARTBEAT expires — with the tab open and sending heartbeats, the session stays alive without a ceiling, as always (whoever is looking is not an idle conversation). The stateless human chat's answer to a turn that STARTED with the session open comes in even if it closes midway (the actor is the model, and the spend has already been measured). deploy/k8s/ does not carry SESSION_CONVERSATION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, and since AT-153 that is a DECISION written in the engine's Deployment, not a pending item: there nothing intercepts the environment, the absence is the runtime.exs default, and writing the number would make a second copy with no guard against diverging — changing the ceiling there is an env: item in the overlay's engine patch. The THREE composes map it with the code's default (the installation one only since AT-153, and until then the line in an installation's .env was inert), guarded by scripts/ci/teto-ocioso-nos-composes.spec.ts. Since AT-154 the screen handles the 409 with its own sentence (item 11); the screen's other actions that write to a closed session keep showing the api's message.

    The repository is born on accepting the handoff to the Arquiteto, and execution does not start without it (RN-582)

    RN-582 — Accepting the handoff to the Arquiteto provisions the repository; accepting to the Dev Lead is the second, idempotent door; and execution/activate without a repository is a named 409

    It revises the TRIGGER of RN-522, which fulfilled the promise of RN-541. The mechanism does not change — the same ProvisionRepositoryUseCase, called by the same AcceptHandoffUseCase, always local, with the failure becoming repository.provision_failed and never taking down the acceptance. Structural decision in ADR 0165.

    What the real installation showed (AT-092, v6.1.0, 2026-09-14). The Arquiteto proposed open_adr_pr three times before the repository existed; the handoffs to infra and dev-lead were offered together, only the infra one was accepted, and POST /projects/:id/execution/activate answered 201. The tables project_repositories, project_git_connections and repo_bootstraps stayed empty — the project without a repository forever. Two defects: the trigger came AFTER those who need the repository (Arquiteto and Infra Lead write to it before the Dev Lead), and the only trigger was SKIPPABLE (activating execution does not require accepting to the Dev Lead).

    1. The trigger is accepting the handoff to arquiteto. The Arquiteto is only activated by an accepted handoff addressed to it (canActivateAgent), and that handoff is born from the PO (offer_handoff(to_agent: "arquiteto")) or from the user (manual handoff) — both doors go through the same acceptance. Provisioning runs BEFORE activateAgent: the Arquiteto wakes up in a project that already has somewhere to write. Consequence: the Infra Lead, activated by a handoff FROM the Arquiteto, never again wakes up without a repository.

    2. Accepting to dev-lead keeps provisioning, as a SECOND DOOR. It is the way out for a project that went through the Arquiteto before this rule (the exp001 of AT-092: Arquiteto accepted, Dev Lead offered) and the natural resumption of a provisioning that failed at the acceptance to the Arquiteto. With the created repository already up, the second call creates nothing — no repository, no session, no bootstrap row, no branch, no commit —, and that is proven by BOTH doors in sequence against the real Postgres and LocalGitProvider.

    3. execution/activate without a repository is REFUSED with 409, right after the module_map check and BEFORE any effect (persisted budget, permissions.json, session, engine, event). The sentence is chosen by the state of the project's handoffs, read by HandoffRepository.findByProject (from all sessions — the handoff to the Arquiteto lives in the PO's): handoff to the Arquiteto offered → accept it; otherwise to the Dev Lead offered → accept it; otherwise one of the two already accepted → provisioning left no repository, see the repository.provision_failed and use the provisioning page (/projects/:id/provisioning?provider=local); otherwise → no handoff to the Arquiteto was accepted. A handoff offered to ANOTHER agent never becomes an acceptance instruction (accepting the Infra provisions nothing). An ADOPTED repository counts as a repository. Refusing and not provisioning here is a decision: provisioning inside activation would hide a git effect, and the agents before it would remain without a repository.

    4. The screen removes the control and states the reason once, in text (the rule of RN-102 and ADR 0064). In the Execution section of the Overview, with GET .../git/repository answering a CONFIRMED null, "Activate execution" stays inert in place, the text says where the repository is born, and there is a link to provision. On the card of the handoff to the Dev Lead, inside the session, the "Activate execution" shortcut leaves and the card says that accepting that handoff provisions the repository. Loading or with an error, nothing locks — "I don't know" does not become "it doesn't have", and the backend refuses anyway. Accepting a handoff invalidates the repository query, because the acceptance may have created it.

    The technical session does not displace the working one (AT-131). The session the provisioning opens (repo_bootstraps.session_id, named git-bootstrap) is born in the MIDDLE of the Arquiteto's phase, and choosing "the most recent" only by createdAt put it in place of the working session until the next one was born (ADR 0165 left that declared). Now the two reads by createdAt of the workspace summary (latestSessionId and the cut of the unread ones) order by "is a bootstrap session" BEFORE createdAt, and the Overview (useLatestSession) does the same. The technical one is only the most recent when it is the ONLY one — in the manual provisioning flow it is in it that the project starts. The api reads the marker through repo_bootstraps; the web only has the session's NAME, and renaming it makes the two diverge (the Overview then treats the summary as being of another session and does not use it). The criterion does not change what ADR 0165 decided (where the repository is born), which is why there is no new ADR.

    Revised by RN-592 (AT-183): the web stopped reading the NAME — the session listing returns the technical marker, through the same link in repo_bootstraps, and renaming the session no longer makes the two diverge.

    The activation refusal does not tell to accept a handoff from a closed session (RN-581, AT-131). Accepting a handoff in a terminal session is 409 sessao_encerrada, checked BEFORE the handoff becomes accepted — so nothing is half provisioned. The refusal sentence now queries the state of the session of each offered handoff: only the one living in an OPEN session becomes "accept it"; if the only offered one is in a closed session, the sentence says so and points to the provisioning page. A session not found counts as open ("I don't know" does not become "closed"). The events provisioning writes do not fall under RN-581: the actor is system and the destination is the freshly created git-bootstrap session. What remains NOT covered: the Overview and the handoff card in the session read the state of the repository, not that of each session, and did not change.

    RN-583 — O critério de roteamento do hub é do binding, viaja com ele, e congela no metering

    Um binding de modelo pode guardar um critério de roteamento — routing_preference: price, throughput ou latency — que diz ao HUB como escolher o upstream que serve o modelo. Anulável: null é o comportamento de sempre, nada vai ao fio e o hub decide sozinho.

    1. Viaja com o binding que venceu, nunca cascateia sozinho. A cascata continua sendo de binding: o nível vencedor traz o modelo E o critério dele. O nível que a cascata PULA (modelo indisponível, sem tool calling) leva o critério junto — sobreviver só o critério produziria combinação que ninguém escolheu.
    2. Escrita em três formas. No PUT .../model-binding dos cinco escopos, routingPreference ausente preserva o gravado se o provider do modelo novo declara a capability, e vira null se não declara; null limpa; valor para provider sem a capability é 422 (RoutingPreferenceNotSupportedError). Invariante: nenhum binding guarda critério para provider que não o declara.
    3. Congela o que FOI AO FIO. token_usage.routing_preference é gravado por chamada, ao lado do upstream_provider da RN-042: o critério enviado, e null quando o binding não tinha ou quando o provider não declara a capability (o que não foi enviado não é procedência de nada). Mesma régua do preço congelado (ADR 0042).
    4. Capability de PROVIDER, só com prova. LLMProviderCapabilities.routingPreference é obrigatória nos nove, e é true SÓ no OpenRouter desde 2026-09-29 (AT-158): o smoke com credencial real (openrouter-provider.roteamento.smoke.spec.ts) mostrou o critério MUDANDO o upstream que serviu — em meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct, price pousou na DeepInfra e throughput na Groq (latency foi Groq numa medição e CoreWeave na outra), enquanto sem critério o hub alternou Novita/DeepInfra. A prova é a DIFERENÇA, não o aceite: o modelo do default antigo (~deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-latest) devolveu o MESMO upstream para os três critérios e sem critério, e isso não distingue "o hub respeitou" de "não havia escolha". Os outros oito seguem false, e para eles a feature continua DORMENTE: a rota recusa com 422, a tela diz em texto que o provider não tem a opção provada, e nada muda no fio. O que a prova NÃO afirma: qual upstream cada critério escolhe — isso é decisão do hub e muda com o tempo.

    RN-590 — The artifacts' docs/ folder is rebuilt from the event log by the SAME translator as the live projector, without touching the outbox, and never comes out as a silent success

    ADR 0148 called the docs/ folder rebuildable and declared, in cost 3, that there was no reprojection command: deleting the folder did not rebuild it, because the outbox rows were already marked. It is the same gap RN-569 closed for the graph, in a second consumer. Measured by reading the code: a Postgres restore, the loss of the project_workspaces volume and the execution_mode conversion (which does not touch docs/) leave the folder absent or in the old place, and nothing rewrites it.

    The rule: apps/api/src/scripts/reprojetar-artefatos.ts (pnpm --filter api artefatos:reprojetar; node scripts/reprojetar-artefatos.js in the image) sweeps session_events and rewrites the folder. As in RN-569:

    1. A single translator. The event → agent folder, file name and Markdown translation LEFT ArtifactProjector for ArtifactEventTranslator; the projector reaches the event through an outbox row, the reprojection through a cursor, and both call it. The projector's surface (constructor, drainOnce) did not change. The list of what is projected remains ARTIFACT_PROJECTABLE_EVENT_TYPES — a new type goes in there and is translated in the same place, never in a second translator.
    2. Idempotent and never deletes. The name is a function of the event (versioned: <tipo>.md; append-only: with the seq), so running again rewrites the same files; resuming is running again, or --after-event from the printed cursor. A file the user put in docs/ stays.
    3. It does not touch the outbox (aggregate_type = 'artifact_projection'): it runs with the api up without stealing, reopening or marking rows.
    4. Never a silent success. Unlike the graph, there is no destination that stops everything (a write failure belongs to the ITEM, ADR 0148): each failure is counted and named with the event's id, the rest is written, and the process exits with 1. A nonexistent --project is refused without writing.

    What this rule does NOT close: (a) the versioned ones (module_map, module_routing, project_image, c4_diagram) show the LAST event in id order; --after-event starting between two versions may leave an older one — only the full round guarantees the current one; (b) it writes to the project's CURRENT location, and needs to see the same disk as the api; (c) it does not recreate qa_verdict/secops_verdict/task_blocked/infra_delegation_files, which were never a file; (d) no time measurement on a large event log; (e) it does NOT go into backup — it is derived, the argument of ADR 0152.

    RN-592 — The session listing says which one is the technical one, through the link in repo_bootstraps, and the screen reads the marker instead of the name

    RN-582 (AT-131) made the provisioning's technical session — that of repo_bootstraps.session_id — stop displacing the working session as "the most recent", but with TWO criteria: the api recognized it by the link in repo_bootstraps, and the web by the NAME (git-bootstrap).     1. The api returns the marker. Each item of GET /projects/:projectId/sessions carries technical: boolean (SessionListItemResponseDto), true only for the session of repo_bootstraps.session_id of THAT project (one per project, unique(project_id)). It is the SAME criterion as the workspace summary (sessaoTecnicaDeBootstrap), never the name: renaming does not change the marker, and a working session called git-bootstrap does not become technical.
    2. Only the listing carries it. The marker is not a column of sessions nor a field of the Session entity: the GET of a session and the responses of create/rename/transition stay with SessionResponseDto, without it. It is the listing the screen sorts to find "the most recent".
    3. The screen reads the marker. sessaoMaisRecente (useLatestSession) skips the session with technical: true and only returns it when it is the ONLY one — the rule of RN-582 unchanged, with the source swapped. The web's SessaoListada type takes the field from the OpenAPI GENERATED type.

    What it does NOT close: the Overview and the handoff card in the session still do not query the state of each handoff's session (the gap RN-582 declared); deciding whether they start querying it is a separate decision, outside this rule.

    RN-595 — Every _PREVIOUS a service reads reaches it through the three composes, empty by default

    The three zero-downtime rotations (AUTH_JWT_SECRET, BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN, CREDENTIALS_MASTER_KEY) depend on the process seeing the old value in a _PREVIOUS variable during the window. Compose does not pass the host environment through, and none of the three was in the environment: of any compose: setting the _PREVIOUS in .env had no effect, and whoever followed the runbook performed, without knowing, the dry swap that rotation exists to avoid. Now the api receives the three, and the engine and the broker receive BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN_PREVIOUS, in the dev, production and installation composes, always with an EMPTY default — set means rotation in progress, and a filled default would leave the installation forever in the middle of one. Empty is the same as absent in the three readers.

    RN-597 — Changing the pepper is a global logout

    The pepper that keys the HMAC of opaque tokens has no _PREVIOUS, and changing it has a consequence, not a procedure: every refresh token in circulation, every open e-mail verification and password reset link, and every personal access token (PAT) can no longer be found, because the hash recomputed with the new pepper does not match the stored one. The refused refresh records refresh_unknown (and not refresh_reuse_detected), the link says "Link inválido ou expirado", and the lockout buckets change key — a locked account unlocks. The PASSWORD survives (argon2id with per-record salt, no pepper): changing the pepper costs a login, never an account, and the api starts normally with the new value.

    Until RN-613, a pepper without its own value fell back to AUTH_JWT_SECRET, and rotating the JWT was also rotating the pepper, with all the consequences above. Since then the pepper is mandatory in production and never borrowed from the JWT.

    • Where: apps/api/src/infrastructure/security/auth-key-material.ts:212 (pepper), :228 (hashDeToken), :247 (baldeDeEmail); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/auth/pat-auth.guard.ts:142

    RN-603 — Auto mode releases the path scope, and only it

    Product owner decision on 2026-09-26 (AT-226, ADR 0167): with "Modo automático" on for an agent — the "*" wildcard of RN-153 resolved as auto_approve —, the agent runs ANY terminal command without asking for approval, INCLUDING outside the project folder. The path scope ceiling of ADR 0055 stops holding for that agent. Measured on exp001 (mounted mode, container up): 51 commands asked for approval with the mode on, 47 only for citing /work or /tmp — the dev agent runs in the container and the scope compares against the HOST root.

    decide() starts receiving the ORIGIN of the autonomy (ctx.autonomyOrigin: 'especifica' or 'curinga'), resolved by the SAME repository that already resolved the precedence — findMode became a read of resolve, not a second rule. Only the wildcard in auto_approve is auto mode (modoAutomaticoDoAgente); an absent origin counts as specific. In auto mode, two prompts cease to exist: the SCOPE ceiling and the require_approval that the COMPOUND command synthesizes when a segment has no rule at all in permissions.json (the file with no opinion, which never downgrades an earlier stage) — without the second, cd /work && npm test would keep asking.

    Everything remains as it was, in auto mode too: deny (from the file, from the built-in patterns or from specific autonomy) wins; an ask WRITTEN in the file asks; the external-effect/privileged-command ceiling (push, PR, deploy, sudo/doas, RN-418) runs first and does not look at the origin; merge into a protected branch, instruction_patch, parallelize/raise_max_parallel and container_remove are never auto-approvable (RN-154). A specific rule for the type beats the wildcard in the repository and arrives as 'especifica': terminal: require_approval with the wildcard on keeps asking. Turning off (the agent card's toggle writes the wildcard as require_approval) restores the ceiling. Since RN-670 (ADR 0189) the specific auto_approve under the auto_approve wildcard — what a dev agent's "Sempre permitir" writes — resolves as the WILDCARD, and no longer turns off auto mode; and, outside it, the scope compares against the REAL execution folder (RN-669).

    RN-604 — The call to the broker has a ceiling PER OPERATION, and the blown ceiling says it was the ceiling

    The broker's HTTP client applied ONE ceiling, 5 s, to the five operations. The docblock justified it by the screen READ path (RN-486), and it also held for exec — whose request CARRIES its own timeoutMs — and for start, which waits for the docker run and the image pull it does. Reproduced in AT-233: a fake broker answering an exec in 6 s, with a timeoutMs of 8 s, came back as BrokerIndisponivelError('sem-resposta') — "the container broker did not answer … The operation was aborted due to timeout". That is, every terminal command over 5 s in a container/mounted project with a running container (RN-492) failed saying the broker was down, while the command kept running.

    And the engine cut too: the container-exec call did not pass receive_timeout and fell back to Req's default, 15 s — the SAME default as TERMINAL_ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS. Reproduced with a fake api (Bandit) that answers in 16 s: {:error, %Req.TransportError{reason: :timeout}}. Raising the ceiling only in the api would fix nothing.

    The rule:

    1. inspect stays short (5 s) — it is the read of /containers and of the lifecycle route, and a screen that waits for the broker's worst case is worse than one that declares "not observed".
    2. exec DERIVES from timeoutMs (or from the broker's 15 s default, when it comes without one): broker context (10 s) + ps (30 s) + the larger of the command and the diagnostic docker version (30 s) + 5 s of margin. The broker cuts the command at timeoutMs and ANSWERS timedOut: true; the api has to be waiting when the answer arrives.
    3. start/stop/remove wait for the broker's OWN worst case: context + ps + the operation (the run with the pull; the stop with the 10 s of grace; rm --force) + the docker version it runs when it fails, plus the margin. Waiting for that is waiting for the broker's ANSWER, including its named refusal. The math was born with 105 s and forgot the SECOND ps of the resolver (the managed one and the namesake): the real worst case was 130 s. Since RN-605 it counts the six control calls of start and gives 195 s.
    4. The engine waits longer than the api: timeoutMs + 90 s. The chain is broker < api < engine, and the tests on both sides check it (the api mirrors the engine's slack as FOLGA_DO_EXEC_NO_ENGINE_MS, and the engine's test reads that number from the api's source).
    5. A blown ceiling has its own reason: BrokerIndisponivelError gains teto-excedido, distinct from sem-resposta (connection refused, DNS), and the message names the operation and the number — and, in the long ones, the consequence: the command may keep running in the container; the run/pull may have happened, so check /containers before repeating. In the screen's read teto-excedido falls into the SAME naoObservado: 'broker-sem-resposta' as always, with the text in detalhe — no new value in the DTO.

    The numbers on the other side (TIMEOUT_DE_CONTROLE_MS, TIMEOUT_DE_EXEC_PADRAO_MS, the TIMEOUT_MS of the broker's context client) are MIRRORED in named constants, not imported: the api does not consume the Docker port package. Nothing changes in the broker's containment (ADR 0130), in DockerPort nor in RN-502.

    Declared, not closed:

    • A pull of more than 30 s keeps failing — in the broker. The pull runs under the Docker port's TIMEOUT_DE_CONTROLE_MS (30 s), and a big image does not come up on the first attempt. Since RN-605 the overflow has a NAME (PullExcedeuTetoError, origin infra) instead of "code -1" with origem: null; the ceiling itself did not go up, by the maintainer's decision.

    • Node's fetch waits for headers for at most 300 s. An exec with timeoutMs above ~255 s is cut by undici before this rule's ceiling; the error comes out teto-excedido naming the 300 s. The outer hop (/internal/actions/execute, api → engine) also has no explicit ceiling and falls into the same 300 s, so TERMINAL_ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS above ~210 s does not arrive whole.

    • A sick broker at ps (the docker ps taking the whole 30 s and the diagnosis another 30) may exceed the exec ceiling with a short command; it comes out teto-excedido, with the right name.

    RN-609 — proposed_action.created says WHICH root the scope compared, relative and never absolute

    RN-567 put in the event the RULE that decided (reason) and declared what stayed out: point 7 of ADR 0055 asks for which scope authorized, and escopo: cd dentro da pasta do projeto does not say which folder the scope was that day. The root changes — mode conversion, a new base —, and the event is the only place that keeps what held at the instant of the decision.

    The rule: the payload of the SESSION event proposed_action.created of a terminal action gains scopeRoot, with three fields — executionMode, ancora and segmento:

    mode ancora segmento
    container raiz_gerenciada the workspace_dir_name — the root IS <PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT>/<segmento>
    mounted base_de_projetos the piece under BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE, through the SAME segmentoSobABaseDeProjetos the broker uses
    mounted (without a base, outside it, or the base itself) indisponivel null
    runner nome_da_pasta the workspace_dir_name — identifies the folder without being relative to anything the server knows

    Never the absolute path, and that is the decision (AT-147, the maintainer's). The event log is read by every project member and an event is not rewritten; in mounted/runner the root is a folder on the user's machine, with their $HOME in the path. That is why indisponivel exists: falling back to the absolute path "so as not to lose information" would be exactly the leak. In runner the agent's local base never crosses the network, so there is no relative segment the server can compute — the ancora says the value is a NAME and not a path.

    Only in terminal. It is the only type in which decide() consults the scope (terminalNoEscopo); in the others the field does not exist, instead of existing saying something the decision did not use. The derivation is that of projectScopeRoot — raizDoEscopoNoEvento lives next to it, in the same file, and it is not a second rule: what it does is EXPRESS the same root without the absolute part.

    Additive, and absent is not "no root". An event written before this rule, or of another type, does not have the field; there is no reprocessing nor new column. The outbox does not carry it, for the same reason as RN-567 (no consumer in the engine). Nothing in decide() changes, no ceiling, and the screen does not change — where it shows up is another delivery (AT-148). (Since RN-614 the root shows up together with the reason, on the event's line in the log panel and in the ApprovalCard, always relative and with its own text for indisponivel.) The web reads the payload as a generic record, so old and new events go through the same read.

    Declared: in mounted, the segment is relative to the base configured AT THE INSTANT of the decision — if the base changes later, the old segment keeps saying what was true then, which is the point. And the separation between scope and permissions.json (RN-478) does not go into the field: it describes the SCOPE's root, never where the policy file lives.

    RN-611 — The MACHINE key gains listing and revocation per ACCOUNT, without :projectId: only the machine ones, only the user's own, and the revocation is the SAME as always

    The gap RN-552 and RN-561 declared in writing: "in an installation that has no PROJECT yet, listing and revocation — both via /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys — have no project to answer against". The one-line installation (RN-547) creates EXACTLY that situation: the account and the machine key are born before any project, and the key stayed alive and unreachable. The maintainer's decision (AT-118): yes, in the Account.

    Two new routes, and only two. GET /users/me/machine-device-keys lists and DELETE /users/me/machine-device-keys/:deviceKeyId revokes (204, idempotent). No @RequireRole, like users/me/credentials and users/me/preferences: the scope is the person THEMSELF, and there is no project nor workspace to resolve a role against. The userId comes from the session JWT and goes into the WHERE; no parameter names another person, and the maintainer view over someone else's key stays out by the decision of RN-519 — this route does not reopen it through another door.

    Only the MACHINE kind. The listing returns ONLY project_id IS NULL (especie: "maquina"), revoked ones INCLUDED (the rule of RN-519: making the row disappear would make the screen assert the key never existed). The PROJECT ones have a home — their project's device-keys section, where the reach of revoking them is stated — and bringing them into the Account would make the Account take down a project's pairing without naming the project. For the same reason, revocation via the account refuses a PROJECT key with 404, the SAME response as for a key that does not exist or belongs to another person: the question goes to the SAME listing as the screen, filtered by userId, so there is no way to ask about someone else's key and learn that it exists.

    What revoking actually takes down, and the target does NOT change. Revocation via the account is not a new revocation: RevokeMachineDeviceKeyUseCase checks that the key is among the caller's machine ones and DELEGATES to RevokeRunnerDeviceKeyUseCase, byte for byte. It writes the row and, for the machine key, asks the engine for a disconnectRunnerOfUser per project in runner mode the owner reaches (RN-520/RN-543). The target remains {projeto, usuário} and never {chave}: another runner of the same user in those projects drops along, even with a PAT or another key, and reconnects if its credential is still valid. In an installation without a project, the list of projects is empty and the revocation only writes the row — and that is enough: the machine agent waiting for the first project (RN-550) has no connection at all to take down, and the next ticket it asks for is refused. Changing the target remains its own front, with an ADR (AT-013).

    "Registering replaces the previous one" STAYS. RN-552 had two reasons to revoke the previous machine key on each registration: (a) the service token cannot manufacture durable credentials in series, and a reinstalled machine cannot leave behind a live key nobody remembers to revoke; (b) the orphan would be UNREACHABLE. This RN knocks down (b) and leaves (a) intact — it does not depend on a screen. What changes is that the replaced one now SHOWS UP, revoked, in the Account; and since nobody revoked it through the screen, the section says in TEXT that reinstalling revokes the previous one, so the row is not read as an incident.

    The screen lives in the Account (/account), the page that already existed for what follows the person across projects. It lists name, creation date, last use and status, and inherits the WHOLE vocabulary of RN-561/RN-548: lastUsedAt is RECORDED use, never connection, and null has its own text ("never used"); "active"/"revoked" talks about the ROW and never about an agent up — and "active" is not green, because the machine kind never gets green and there there are only those. There is no kind column: with a single kind it would repeat the same word on every row, and what it carried in the project section — the REACH — is stated in the caption and in the confirmation ("takes down the local agent in ALL your projects in runner mode; with no project at all, it only prevents the key from being used again"), together with RN-520's collateral cost. Loading, failed, empty, revoked and never used are five states with five texts (RN-088/RN-470). With no minimum role on the endpoint, the screen does not invent one: roleAtLeast here would lock out whoever can, the worse defect of the two.

    Revoking through one list invalidates ALL of them. The machine key shows up in the Account's list (['machine-device-keys']) and in that of EVERY project of the owner (['runner-device-keys', projectId], read by RunnerOnboardingPanel and by the device-keys section). invalidarChavesDeDispositivo invalidates the per-project one by PREFIX (every project in the cache) and the Account's always, and BOTH revocation screens call it — before, revoking through the project section invalidated only that of the open project, and the other lists kept announcing the revoked one.

    RN-613 — AUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER is mandatory and its own; whoever migrates sets it with the current AUTH_JWT_SECRET

    The HMAC pepper of opaque tokens (refresh, account links, PATs, lockout bucket) no longer falls back to AUTH_JWT_SECRET. The silent fallback (AUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER ?? passphraseAtual()) turned every "zero-downtime" JWT rotation into a pepper change, and it was the COMMON path: the production and installation composes did not even pass the variable through. In production the api REFUSES to start without it, and the refusal states the fix — "defina com o valor ATUAL de AUTH_JWT_SECRET para não deslogar ninguém" —, because the obvious fix (generating a random one) is the one that logs everyone out. With the pepper equal to the old JWT the hash is byte for byte the previous one, refresh tokens and PATs remain valid, and from then on the JWT rotates on its own. A pepper equal to the JWT is NOT refused: it is the legitimate state of every migrated installation. The JWT rules (RN-114) apply: blank, the two example literals from the repository and fewer than 16 characters bring down the boot. Outside production a development default of its OWN applies (dev-auth-token-pepper-change-me), never the JWT's.

    The install.sh does the migration: a NEW installation generates a random pepper; if there is a previous .env in the folder, it is READ (never executed) before being overwritten, and its pepper is kept — or, without a pepper, it is born with its AUTH_JWT_SECRET. The terminal says where the value came from, never the value.

    RN-615 — WORKSPACE member removal is born with ceiling 2 inherited: removing oneself is 403, and it is that clause that holds the last owner, without counting

    The fifth door of the ceilings line (RN-472, RN-556, RN-557), and the route ADR 0157 refused to open in passing. Until now WorkspacesController had no member @Delete, and offboarding was a write to the database. The maintainer's decision (AT-115/HS-006): the route is born, protected by a CLAUSE.

    The route. DELETE /workspaces/:workspaceId/members/:userId, owner (the SAME minimum as the upsert), 204, idempotent.

    The ceiling is inherited, with no new rule. remocaoEhAutoRebaixamento receives the actor's WORKSPACE role as today's effective one and null as the AFTER role — in the workspace there is no level above to catch the fall, so removing one's own row is always a fall to "no access", the branch the function already stated for a project without a workspace row. Removing ONESELF is always 403, with its own sentence: "Você não pode remover a si mesmo deste workspace: aqui não há papel acima para segurar a queda, e sem a linha você perde o workspace e todos os projetos dele. Voltar exige o owner que você estaria abandonando. Peça a outro owner."

    The last owner, by the SAME clause. Only owner calls the route; nobody removes themselves; so every successful removal leaves at least the CALLER as owner. Removing the last one would require them to remove themselves — the refused movement. The count stays refused (ADR 0157, point 2). The route's owner minimum is HALF of the proof, and that is why it is asserted in a test.

    movement outcome
    removing ONESELF from the workspace, whether or not there is another owner 403
    removing ANOTHER owner passes — it is how ownership is revoked entirely
    removing the HOLDER (created_by), by another owner 409 criador_do_workspace — RN-616
    removing any other person passes
    removing someone with no workspace row 204 — their project rows in the workspace go out the same

    The cascade, in one transaction. The workspace_members row; the project_members rows of the removed person in THIS workspace's projects (without them the projectRole ?? workspaceRole overlay of RN-471 would keep them inside every project in which they had their own row); and their credentials tied to those projects — PROJECT device keys and PATs —, revoked with the reason workspace_member_removed. After the commit, their runner's live connection drops in EACH project of the workspace through the path of RN-520, in a try/catch that only logs: an engine down does not take down the removal.

    Declared and NOT done: the MACHINE key (it belongs to the account and serves other workspaces; here it stops reaching because the role resolves to none); the already connected SESSION socket and the removed person's :web terminal (they stay until they drop; the new ticket is refused); a screen (there is no workspace members section in the apps/web). The HOLDER (workspaces.created_by) does not leave through this route — that is RN-616.

    RN-616 — The workspace HOLDER does not leave through member removal: 409 criador_do_workspace until transferring, and holdership only goes to another owner

    The maintainer's decision on the question RN-615 left open (AT-115, ADR 0173, point 7). workspaces.created_by authorizes nothing — what authorizes is the role (RN-472) —, but it is through it that the LLM credential the agents spend and the git one of agent actions are resolved (RN-058), as well as the owner of the spend report (RN-060). Removing the creator would leave the agents spending the credential of someone no longer in the workspace. The column comes to be called, in the rule, the holder.

    The refusal. DELETE /workspaces/:workspaceId/members/:userId with target = holder is 409 with code: "criador_do_workspace": "Não é possível remover o titular do workspace: a credencial de LLM que os agentes gastam, a de git das ações de agente e o relatório de gasto são dele (RN-058/RN-060). Transfira antes a titularidade para outro owner (PUT /workspaces/:workspaceId/owner-of-record) e remova depois." RN-615's ceiling comes first: the holder trying to remove themselves gets the self-removal 403.

    The transfer. PUT /workspaces/:workspaceId/owner-of-record, owner, body { userId }, answers the workspace (200). The destination must ALREADY be owner of the workspace, otherwise 409 titular_precisa_ser_owner ("A titularidade só vai para quem já é owner deste workspace: o titular paga o que os agentes gastam (RN-058). Promova a pessoa a owner antes, ou escolha outro owner."). It writes created_by in a transaction with the role read; transferring to the current holder is idempotent. Any owner can transfer, including to ANOTHER owner who did not ask — declared, it is the same authority that removes owners.

    The spend, from the commit on. ResolveCredentialOwnerUseCase returns the new holder: the agent turn looks for THEIR credential for the model's provider, and git actions for their git credential. Without a credential, the outcome is the one that already existed — the turn ends with "Nenhuma credencial cadastrada para " and the git remote read fails naming whose credential is missing. The transfer does NOT check this beforehand (declared in the ADR). The recorded spend does not move: token_usage does not keep the holder, and the whole report, history included, comes to belong to the new holder. No domain event: there remains a log line with from/to/who.

    The language of the agents' answers (RN-618..620, RN-622..624, ADR 0177)

    Epic EP-028 was born from a conversation in Portuguese answered in Spanish. The maintainer's decisions of 2026-09-28 (AT-168, AT-169) fixed where the language of the ANSWERS lives — account, session and project — and the precedence among the sources. None of these rules touches the INTERFACE language (RN-432).

    RN-618 — The answers' language belongs to the PERSON: a choice in the account, an override per session, and the precedence that always ends in a language

    1. Open list, canonical form. The answers' language is any BCP-47 code whose language subtag the api's ICU recognizes, written canonically (pt-br becomes pt-BR) — never the interface's pt-BR/en enum, which stays closed. und, private use and free text are refused with a 400 that names the rule.
    2. A new account is born on AUTOMATIC. users.response_language is NULL ("automatic") until the person chooses; the api shows and accepts automatico as the name of that state.
    3. Interface and answers are independent. PATCH /users/me/preferences accepts locale and responseLanguage as OPTIONAL; sending one does not touch the other, a body with neither is 400, and an invalid responseLanguage refuses the WHOLE body before writing any field.
    4. The detected one only holds when confirmed. The language detected from the person's messages (detection is RN-624) only goes into users.detected_language together with detected_language_confirmed_at — a CHECK refuses one without the other. Detection alone changes nothing.
    5. A session override belongs only to whoever set it. PUT projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId/response-language (developer, the role for sending a message to an agent — the override only changes the answers to the person's own messages) sets a language in that session for WHOEVER CALLS; language: null (mandatory key) releases it and goes back to inheriting from the account. The GET (viewer) returns the caller's effective one. The key is the session×user pair: another participant of the same session is never affected, and there is no route to read or touch another person's.
    6. The precedence, resolved per person and never per session: session override > account choice > confirmed detected > users.locale. Since users.locale is NOT NULL, the chain always ends in a language, and the origin (sessao/conta/detectado/interface) travels with it. A one-off request inside a message ("translate to English") is not a step: what serves it is the model.

    Who consumes: since RN-622 the effective one reaches the model — the api calls ResolverIdiomaDaRespostaUseCase with the AUTHOR of each message to an agent and the session, and the engine puts the guidance at the end of each LLM call of that turn. The Account stopped saying the value "does not reach yet".

    RN-624 — The api detects the author's language from their own messages and ASKS; only the confirmed one becomes a preference

    RN-618 left the "confirmed detected" step ready and empty. Maintainer decision (AT-168 answers 4, 6 and 7): detect, ASK whether the language is right, and the confirmed one becomes the default — per person, global, with the question on the screen where the language is already shown and corrected.

    1. The yardstick is ONE, and lives in the api. The heuristic of AT-080, measured by AT-160 (contrastive markers of pt/es/en, the stripping of code, log, quotation, URL and identifier), moved from scripts/idioma/ to apps/api/src/domain/iam/heuristica-de-idioma.ts, and the instrument REEXPORTS it from there — what the product runs is what the instrument measures. The rule of WHAT counts as evidence (only actor user; in the form, only the answers, and the echo with the agent's labels skipped) is also a single one, evidenciasDoAutor, used by the real-corpus extraction and by the detection. Local, no LLM, no new dependency.
    2. The sample comes from the event log, the hysteresis is recomputed. Detection reads the person's 11 most recent pieces of evidence across ALL sessions (the window of 10 plus the one the hysteresis recomputes) and decides when the TWO last evaluations of the sample point to the same language (idiomaConcordante). No detection state is stored: the evaluation of the previous message is recomputed with the window that ended at it. The read is served by a PARTIAL index (session_events_evidencia_de_idioma_idx, actor user and the two evidence types): measured with 200 thousand events, 0.056 ms through the index against 13.5 ms for the scan without it.
    3. The thresholds are PROVISIONAL. PARAMETROS_PROVISORIOS are the candidates of AT-080 with ONE difference, the minimum evidence of 10 words and not 20 — in the SYNTHETIC corpus, at 10 the coverage of decidable cases goes from 42.2% to 58.9% with the same three errors (all in a language outside the three). List at080; threshold 0.8, margin 0.3, sample 10 messages / 2,000 characters, hysteresis 2. The synthetic corpus was written by the same hand that wrote the heuristic: none of these numbers is calibrated, and the owner recalibrates them with the real corpus (pnpm --filter @brabo/scripts idioma:medir --real), changing the object, which is the only place the api reads them from.
    4. When it asks. GET .../sessions/:sessionId/response-language returns detectionQuestion with the language to ask about, or null. It does not ask when: the detection does not agree (short text, "ok", code, log, mixed); the effective one comes from an EXPLICIT choice — session override or Account —, because confirming would record a step BELOW them and the reply would not change; the detected one is already the effective one, compared by SUBTAG (pt does not diverge from pt-BR — the heuristic only knows the language); or the person already declined that language.
    5. Detection never changes anything on its own. Only POST /users/me/preferences/detected-language writes: confirm writes the pair detected_language + detected_language_confirmed_at (the CHECK of RN-618) and deletes the old decline of the same language — and it is 409 deteccao_mudou, without writing, when the messages no longer point to the language (the column says "detected" and cannot hold what the heuristic did not detect); decline writes the decline to detected_language_declines (one row per person and language, with the date), and THAT language is not asked about again. What is stored is the language and the person's decision — never country, nationality or proficiency.
    6. Where the question appears. In a small card anchored just below the language indicator of the session bar (RN-620): "Detectamos que você escreve em espanhol (es) — usar espanhol (es) nas respostas?", with "Usar", "Não" and "Agora não". No modal, without covering the composer; "Agora não" only hides it on this screen, without writing, and the question comes back on the next read. Sending a message (or answering a form) rereads the indicator, because the new message is the evidence that can make the question appear.
    7. Failure never blocks anything. Detection runs on the language READ, and not inside SendAgentMessageUseCase: the evidence is already in the event log, the question survives a page reload and appears in any session, and sending the message does not go through it — it gains no latency and has no way to fail because of it. On the read, any failure (database, heuristic) becomes a warning and detectionQuestion: null; the language keeps being shown.
    8. Cost: CPU measured on the synthetic corpus, on this machine — 11.6 µs to clean and classify a message, 110 µs per detection (11 messages, two evaluations), plus the indexed read of item 2. Zero tokens.

    What this rule does NOT close, declared: the heuristic knows three languages, and the language list is open — Galician and French can become es/pt (the synthetic errors), and under this rule the cost is a wrong question, which the person declines. A message in Spanish in a Portuguese window leaves the sample undetermined while it is in it (no question, no change). And the heuristic file cannot have import: the instrument runs it by type stripping, and scripts/idioma/ has its own tsconfig without verbatimModuleSyntax to accept the exports of a CommonJS module.

    Deciding in the chat, where the owner is (RN-626)

    RN-628 — The executed merge closes the PR's task: done, once only

    The QA/SecOps gate ends in awaiting_user and nothing else touched the task's status: in the real use of 09/29 pr-6 was merged three times and the tasks stayed in in_review (AT-275).

    1. After the merge, never in its place. git_merge is still unconditional require_approval (RN-418); the rule runs INSIDE ExecuteGitActionUseCase, in the transaction that records the merge result, and only when the provider returned state: 'merged' (an open PR, or a merge that failed, does not touch the task).
    2. The task is found through the PR that opened it. Every pr_open of the project whose pullRequestId is that of the merged PR and that carries storyTaskId in the payload. A PR without a task (infra, ADR) changes nothing.
    3. Idempotent. TaskRepository.markDoneIfNotDone is an UPDATE … WHERE status <> 'done': a repeated merge of the same PR returns null, does not move it again and does NOT write the event. When it moves, it writes ONE immutable backlog.task_status_changed event (cause: 'pr_merged', pullRequestId, actionId), append-only, with no UPDATE on an events table. No migration.
    4. Declared boundary (AT-249). This rule does NOT refuse merging an already merged PR nor consult gate_status. Refusing the already merged PR (and the repeated proposal) came later, in RN-663, before the merge reaches here; the pending gate, by owner decision, is only a notice on screen.

    RN-630 — Who is active in the session is read from the WHOLE session, not from the last 200 events

    "Who is active" and "who receives the composer" came from the agent.activated seen in the 200-event window (latest: true). In a long session the activations of the Arquiteto and the Infra left the window; handoff offers addressed to them went back to looking acceptable and the "hi" went to the last agent that still appeared. It is the defect class of RN-180 (a silent ceiling makes the screen assert about what it did not read), already closed for the presence of QA/SecOps in RN-568.

    The rule: the project summary (RN-090) returns roster.activatedAgents — the agents with at least one agent.activated in the most recent session, one per agent, the most recently activated (by seq) first. Four decisions:

    1. The source is still the event log. No derived column, no index and no migration: the field enters the SAME per-session scan that already computes executionActivated/gatesEverOpened (array_agg ... filter), so the number of database round trips of the summary does not change (the constant-count spec still holds). The reserved migration 0066 was not used.
    2. No new HTTP per poll. The field travels in the summary the screens already read (RN-579).
    3. The client ADDS it to the window and only trusts it with the summary of the SAME session (latestSessionId === sessionId), as in RN-568: activation is monotonic (an activated agent does not deactivate), so the window only gives false negatives. A summary of another session does not count; with no summary, the window decides alone.
    4. The api says what happened, not who receives. The explicit, visible recipient in the chat (AT-251) and acceptance by handoffId (AT-253) consume this field in the web and are NOT part of this rule.

    Declared gap: this round only delivers the api CONTRACT. apps/web (session-readiness.ts, session-handoffs.ts) keeps reading the window until AT-251/AT-253 start consuming roster.activatedAgents.

    Closed in RN-631 (AT-251): the composer recipient and the handoff offers of the Session screen ADD roster.activatedAgents to the window, with the same-session guard. criativoActive/arquitetoActive (session-readiness.ts) still read only the window.

    RN-635 — One pending handoff offer per target in the project; the one that stops being valid becomes superseded

    handoffs only recorded offered/accepted, with no expiry, supersession or dedupe: a double click on "architecture ready" gave 2× Infra and 2× Dev Lead, and an offer to an already active agent stayed actionable forever (AT-291, ADR 0182).

    1. At most ONE offered per (project, target). decidirOferta decides: with no pending one, it creates; pending in the SAME session and with no new artifact (the new one is null or equal), it returns the existing one (desfecho: ja_oferecido, no row nor event); any other case creates the new one and replaces the pending one (substituiu_oferta) — returning the old one would lose the new artifact, or leave the requester with nothing to accept in the session they are in.
    2. Whoever replaces records. The row becomes superseded and a handoff.superseded event is born (handoffId, toAgent, motivo, substitutaId) in the session of the OLD offer, actor system, even with the session closed. The original handoff.offered is not touched.
    3. Serialized per target. CreateHandoffUseCase runs in a transaction with pg_advisory_xact_lock of the (project, target) pair: two tabs arriving together produce ONE row. Duplicates from before converge on the next offer or activation, with an event; the migration rewrites no row.
    4. An already active agent receives no offer: 409 reason: agente_ja_ativo, without row or event. Active = agent.activated in a NON-terminal session of the project. The message is the text the model reads: offer_handoff passes it on verbatim, and FalhaDeTurno.origem/1 classifies it as politica.
    5. Activating supersedes. ActivateAgentUseCase (acceptance and direct activation) and ActivateExecutionUseCase (per dev-<modulo>) supersede, after activating, every pending offer to the agent in any session of the project; the accepted one is not touched, and a refused activation supersedes nothing.
    6. "Architecture ready" is idempotent. OfferInfraHandoffUseCase does not trigger the target (infra, dev-lead) that already has a pending offer or is active; with both like that, it neither records nor calls the engine (desfecho: ja_oferecido, jaAtendidos with each one's reason).

    RN-637 — The screen reads the TAIL of the session's actions, and the old pending one comes back with it

    GET /projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId/actions ordered by ascending seq with a ceiling of 200, and usePendingActions never paginated: from the 201st action of a session on — which a real execution easily reaches, a dev agent proposes dozens of commands per task — the NEW pending one was outside the only page read and vanished from the thread, the Executores and Aprovações (AT-296), precisely when someone was waiting for it.

    The rule:

    1. The route accepts latest=true and status=pending. latest brings the limit actions with the highest seq, returned in ASCENDING order and without nextCursor, ignoring afterSeq — the same contract as the events' latest (ADR 0021). status only accepts pending (another value is 400, without querying); combined with latest, it brings the newest pending ones without the decided ones taking up the window. Without the two parameters the contract is the previous one.
    2. The screen asks two questions, and the second only when needed. buscarAcoesDaSessao reads the tail (200); only if it comes back FULL does it also request the pending ones and merge by id, in ascending seq. An old pending one that the tail pushed out is still a decision to be made and does not vanish for having waited too long. The short session — the common case — still costs ONE request, and a failing read of pending ones brings the query down (the screen says it failed, never pretends an empty queue — RN-088).

    What this rule does NOT close: with more than 200 PENDING ones in a session, the oldest beyond them stay out (the ceiling is the same limit); and what the thread shows as DECIDED is still the tail — an old decided action, outside the 200 newest, does not appear in the thread. Pending items of the WHOLE project are another read (RN-638).

    1. Same transaction, after the transition. ApproveActionUseCase accepts an aoAprovar that runs INSIDE the decision's transaction, after assertTransition passes and before execution; it is through it that the pattern (permissions.json/allow or agent_autonomy, RN-509) and the permission.granted are recorded. "Approve first, record later" in separate transactions was refused: it would trade the defect for an approved (and even executed) action with the pattern failing afterwards. agent_autonomy and the event are atomic with the decision; permissions.json is a file and does not enter a transaction — it is only written after the transition is valid, and failing to write it undoes the approval. What remains, declared, is the window of the COMMIT failing after the file was written.
    2. The event goes with the recording, and only with it. A pattern that already exists is not rewritten nor narrated again (padraoGravado: false).
    3. An already approved action is a named success. If the transition is refused because the action is already approved/auto_approved/executed/failed, the response is 201 with desfecho: 'ja_aprovada' (the normal path returns 'aprovada'), without executing again, recording the pattern only if it is missing — with the event. An invalid transition coming from EXECUTION, after the decision has been confirmed, does NOT become ja_aprovada: it propagates as always.
    4. A DENIED action is still 409, named (reason: 'acao_ja_recusada'), without recording pattern or event: freeing forever what someone just denied is not idempotency.
    5. Ceilings intact. git push/PR/deploy, sudo/doas (motivoDeRecusaSempreAprovar, RN-418) and container_remove are still refused with 400 BEFORE any state read — including with the action already approved. The pattern is still the action's EXACT one (generalization by verb is AT-257, outside here).
    6. The ceiling TYPES too (AT-320). Measured in the audit of 09/30: the api only refused the git push TYPED in the terminal; the TYPED git_push passed and recorded GitPush() in allow (or module autonomy), and the ApprovalCard offered the button. TIPOS_SEM_SEMPRE_PERMITIR is the SINGLE list — git_push, pr_open, git_merge (whole: the GitMerge() pattern would apply to every target), container_remove, instruction_patch, parallelize, raise_max_parallel — and motivoDeRecusaDoSempreAprovar judges terminal by the command and the rest by type. The refusal is 400 with reason: 'teto_do_sempre_permitir' and actionType. The web hides the button through the copy in apps/web/src/lib/sempre-permitir.ts, checked against the api's by test; a terminal command keeps the button (repeating the parser on screen would be a second yardstick) and receives the api's refusal. When it was born, it did NOT change decide() nor the seeding; since RN-689 both change — git_push/pr_open are in the decide() ceiling and activation seeds only git_commit —, and the pattern the click would record for them would be inert.

    The closed session can be reopened (RN-649/RN-650)

    RN-649 — A closed/closed_abnormally session reopens to active with the log intact, and the previous closing becomes a new event

    RN-001 said the terminal states have no way out. Since ADR 0183 there is ONE, and only one: the reopening, from closed or closed_abnormally to active, through its own path. The GENERIC transition keeps refusing closed → active with 409, and closing → active remains forbidden through any path.

    1. What comes back is the whole session. The event log is not touched — the conversation, the business rules, the answered questions, the handoff offers and acceptances. A conversational agent stopped at closing comes back through the idempotent start_agent on the first message and rebuilds the history (RN-580). The conversation comes in again because the refusal of RN-581 reads the session's state, which is now active.
    2. The previous closing is not erased. The sessions row loses closed_at and termination_reason; the NEW event session.reopened, in the same seq (RN-002) and with the human actor who reopened, carries {from, to, closedAt, terminationReason}. No event is edited nor renumbered, and the kind does not change (RN-097).
    3. A session with execution does not reopen — 409 sessao_com_execucao. Reopening a session with execution.activated would return it to findActiveExecutionSession (RN-139). The owner's decision, confirmed in ADR 0184.
    4. No deadline. Every closed session is reopenable (the owner's decision, ADR 0184).
    5. The engine is called before the transaction, as in activation: its failure leaves the session closed, with no event. Any non-terminal state is 409 sessao_nao_encerrada.
    6. The closing the reopening undid does not stop the live session. The SessionLifecycleWorker reads the session's status and ignores, with a log, the session.closed/session.closed_abnormally job of a session the api already says is non-terminal.
    7. The Psicólogo's second automatic analysis stays blocked by the alreadyAnalyzed that already existed; manual reprocessing continues. The second graph consolidation extends the window of the same Interacao.

    Following live without hammering (RN-639)

    RN-654 — The resolved bindings of all agents and areas come in a single read

    RN-645 measured 49 requests on loading the Configurações tab, and 20 of them were the RESOLVED binding of each agent (17) and of each area (3), one route per key. Three sections read those keys — models per agent, models per area and best models per capability —, and the 300 req/min ceiling is the USER's (RN-579).

    The rule:

    1. GET projects/:projectId/model-bindings/resolved?agents=…&areas=… returns { agents: [{ key, binding }], areas: [{ key, binding }] }, in the requested order and without repetition. Each binding is EXACTLY what the individual route would respond for that key (GET .../agent-bindings/:slug, GET .../area-bindings/:key): the same cascade workspace › projeto › área › agente without a session, the same origins the screen turns into a chain (RN-470), the Criativo inheritance, and null when no level has a model. There is no new cascade: the use case calls ResolveModelBindingUseCase key by key, with the input the individual route would pass.
    2. The minimum role is that of the individual read routes, viewer. Whoever does not reach the project gets the SAME 403.
    3. The read is contained (ADR 0060): the keys come in a comma-separated list, with the slug alphabet (lowercase, digits, -, _), and are at most 64 combined (TETO_DE_CHAVES_NO_LOTE). A malformed key or a batch above the ceiling is 400 naming the reason, never a key silently discarded — the response would assert about fewer keys than the screen requested.
    4. The web reads the batch through ONE queryKey (['model-bindings-resolved', projectId]), served by one request to the three Configurações sections and, since AT-339, also to the Visão geral and the Executores tab (useBindingsDosAgentes): the roster agents the catalog knows come from that SAME key — the cache one tab warmed serves the other without a request —, and those the catalog does not know (the dev-<modulo>) come from ONE extra batch read, under the same prefix and in slices of the same ceiling. Every write of an agent or area binding rereads the whole batch by that PREFIX, which reaches both reads; no per-agent key is left to invalidate. The failure of these reads leaves the agent card without a model — "I don't know", never an asserted model — and does not fall back to the per-agent route.
    5. The batch failure does not become "no model". With a single read, the failure is of all keys at once: the section states the reason ONCE, with the api's sentence and the action to reread, and each row says "não lido" in place of the chain. While the batch does not respond, the row says "lendo…". "Sem modelo em nenhum nível" stays reserved for the null the api asserted.

    Numbers: the tab load dropped from 49 to 30 requests (configuracoes.orcamento.test.tsx, on dev at 94e5dc721d); the idle minute stays at 64, all from the frame. In AT-339, the Executores tab load dropped from 29 to 27 and the Visão geral's from 33 to 31 (duas-abas.orcamento.test.tsx, with the base roster of three agents — with team and modules, the drop is one per card), and going from Configurações to the Visão geral stopped fetching any binding (before, 3).

    What this rule does NOT close: the per-key routes still exist in the api (no screen reads them anymore). A dev-<modulo> whose key exceeds 64 characters would be refused by the batch format, and the read of the extras would fail entirely — not measured on a real project, and declared.

    Reading the workspace members (RN-655)

    RN-655 — GET workspaces/:id/members is viewer, and returns only id, name, e-mail and role

    The session thread (RN-652) only named whoever had a row in project_members; whoever joins the project only through the WORKSPACE role became "Outro membro", because there was no route that read the workspace members (owner decision, AT-335). The route is born next to the three member WRITE routes (POST/DELETE of member and PUT owner-of-record, all owner), and its minimum is NOT theirs: the minimum is the ENDPOINT's (RN-102), and reading the list is not maintaining it. It is viewer, that of the neighbouring reads (GET workspaces/:id, .../projects) and that of GET projects/:id/members, which it completes — whoever opens a session needs to know who spoke in it, and a workspace viewer already sees every project of the workspace.

    The response has the SAME shape as the project read — userId, name, email, role (the WORKSPACE role) — and nothing else: no createdAt, no account state. A nonexistent workspace is 404, and a non-member is refused by the RolesGuard (403). There is still no workspace members SCREEN: the read exists to name, and the write routes remain API-only.

    The policy reason on each Aprovações card (RN-656)

    RN-656 — The session events read filters by actionId, and each card of the Aprovações tab reads its own reason through it

    The action does not keep the policy reason: it lives in proposed_action.created (RN-567, RN-609). The Aprovações tab reads the PROJECT queue (RN-638) and the log of ONE session, so since AT-333 it said in a single note how many actions were left without a reason (RN-614). Owner decision (AT-336): each card shows its OWN.

    What was measured. The two options for the card were an actionId filter on the events read or a route that read the event by action. The filter is the smaller: it reuses the route (GET .../sessions/:sessionId/events, viewer), the DTO and the use case, and the action already carries the sessionId of the session that proposed it. No index or migration is born: the predicate on payload->>'actionId' runs INSIDE the session, which the unique index (session_id, seq) already narrows. A PROJECT read by actionId would require a new route to find the session the card already knows.

    The rule in the api. actionId returns only the events whose payload.actionId is that action, in the requested session — it never crosses sessions. It combines with the other parameters and limit counts only the matching ones; seq stops being contiguous in the page, so whoever filters does NOT derive omitted ones by subtraction (RN-180). Empty is 400: a filter that vanishes with the wrong string would return the whole log to whoever asked for an action's reason.

    The rule on the screen. useDecisoesDaPolitica: an action whose event is in the log the tab ALREADY loaded uses that one, without a request; the others read by action, in their session, with staleTime: Infinity — an event is immutable, so each action costs ONE read while the cache lives and the queue polls without repeating any. Nothing is requested while the tab is still loading its own log. A read that responds WITHOUT the event gives the "motivo não registrado" sentence (never silent); only the read that FAILS leaves the card silent, and that one, and only that one, is what the top note counts ("de N das M ações abaixo"). Since AT-340 the cards of the pending items from OTHER sessions in the chat (RN-626, PendenciasDeOutrasSessoes, also in the Executores tab) go through the SAME hook and the SAME cache: every action there is from another session, so none is covered by the screen's log and each one reads by action — only the DRAWN ones, within the block's card ceiling, and one the Aprovações tab already read costs nothing there (and vice versa). A read that fails also silences the card and is stated once, at the top of the block. The "needs you" panel does NOT use this path: it reads no log and opening it does not trigger a query, so the card there stays silent, as RN-614 already said — a decision, not a gap. No ceiling changes.

POST .../sessions/:id/readiness records, in this order:

    1. readiness.confirmed, actor the person, with the mark { necessidadeValidada: true, aceiteImplicitoDoPo: true } (the mark is what RN-658 reads; an old event, with payload {}, accepts nothing);
    2. the command to the engine (the turn that consolidates the product_brief, RN-142);
    3. only if the engine ACCEPTED the turn, necessity.validated, actor the same person, with productBriefId: null (the brief does not exist yet — it is born from the turn the click triggers), via: 'readiness.confirmed' and the readinessEventId of step 1.

    The engine's refusal (409 turn in progress, 422 no business rule) bubbles up BEFORE step 3: without an accepted turn there is no brief on the way, and the need does NOT stay validated. The gate stays warn (docs/gates.yml) — nothing downstream consults it. The screen no longer has the "Confirmar necessidade validada" button; the enabled button's title says what the click closes, and the success notice says that the PO comes in when the summary is ready.

    RN-658 — The acceptance of the Criativo→PO handoff is implicit in "Estou pronto": the SAME events, with the person as actor and the implicito mark

    Owner decision (09/30, AT-312): the separate click to accept the PO goes away. The Criativo→PO handoff is born AFTER the click (it is the turn the click triggers that offers it, CriativoServer.executar_confirm_readiness/1), so the acceptance does not fit in the click's POST: it happens in the internal route that CREATES the offer (POST /internal/sessions/:id/handoffs), right after CreateHandoffUseCase, and goes through the SAME AcceptHandoffUseCase as the card.

    Measured before changing, acceptance through the card records: the row's transition to accepted, handoff.accepted (actor the person, {handoffId, toAgent}), agent.activated (actor the person, {agent}) and, by RN-635, the handoff.superseded of the other offers to the PO in the project. The implicit acceptance records exactly those, with the SAME human actor — whoever clicked, read from the marked readiness.confirmed —, and adds the mark implicito: { via: 'readiness.confirmed', readinessEventId } in the payload of handoff.accepted and of agent.activated. No event is edited, no system actor takes the person's place, and acceptance through the card stays without the mark.

    It is accepted only when ALL hold (decidirAceiteImplicitoDoPo): the offer is criativo → po, offered, of THIS session, and carries as artifact the product_brief born AFTER the most recent marked readiness.confirmed. Otherwise the offer stays offered and the card appears as always: a session prior to ADR 0185 (no mark), a brief prior to the click, and the MANUAL handoff, which never carries an artifact (RN-633 — "Estou pronto" stays on screen after it). A failed acceptance does NOT bubble up to the engine (the offer was created, and the Criativo would say "I couldn't offer" — false): it becomes a durable agent.error, actor system/aceite-implicito, with origin (infra or politica) and reason: aceite_implicito_falhou. The 400 for "not offered" is not a failure: someone decided the offer through another path in the interval, and that is already in the log. The screen hands the composer recipient to the PO on the click (the gesture of calling him, RN-631); until he joins, the choice does not count and the Criativo keeps receiving. No ceiling moves: accepting the PO does not provision a repository (only the Arquiteto and the Dev Lead, RN-582), does not merge nor push.

    RN-660 — The PO's handoff to the Arquiteto is accepted by the SYSTEM when the backlog is covered and the repository is local and without credentials

    The po → arquiteto offer that the engine creates (POST /internal/sessions/:id/handoffs) is accepted without a click, in the same request and AFTER the offer's transaction, when the four conditions hold (decidirAceiteAutomatico, pure):

    1. the offer is offered;
    2. the backlog is covered: the project has at least ONE business rule (artifact.business_rule) and NONE without a story that cites it in businessRuleIds — the SAME computeCoverage as the Backlog tab and the PO's read (RN-164). Zero rules is not covered;
    3. the repository is local and without credentials: the project has no repository (the acceptance provisions local) or has a local one, and has no git connection (OAuth) in project_git_connections;
    4. whoever opened the session still has developer in the project (effective role, RN-471) — the minimum of the human acceptance route.

    The acceptor is still AcceptHandoffUseCase: the repository is born there, before activateAgent (RN-582, ADR 0165), on behalf of whoever opened the session. The acceptance is auditable: handoff.accepted and agent.activated come out with the SYSTEM actor handoff-auto-accept, and handoff.accepted carries automatico: true, emNomeDe and the criterio (regras, cobertas, repositorio). A condition that fails records nothing — the offer stays with the usual button, and the response to the engine says the reason (regras_sem_historia, repositorio_nao_local, credencial_de_git_no_projeto…). A failure AFTER deciding "yes" does not bubble up: it becomes the handoff.auto_accept_failed event (origin infra) and the thread shows it. With the acceptance done, the offer_handoff tool tells the PO that the Arquiteto has already been activated. A remote repository or one with credentials still asks for the click, and the manual handoff (ADR 0109) too.
