    RN-663 — PR merge refuses the already merged PR and the repeated proposal; a pending gate is only a notice

    The real use of 09/29 measured both holes: pr-6 had THREE git_merge executed, and pr-4 was merged with the task in awaiting_qa. The api did not dedupe git_merge per PR (only the screen did, and only in the same list), and LocalGitProvider returned the already merged PR without error — the executor recorded a second executed for the same merge.

    1. Proposal. A git_merge of a PR that a previous execution already merged (executed with state: 'merged') is 409 pr_ja_mergeado; with a LIVE proposal of the same PR (pending, approved or auto_approved), 409 merge_ja_proposto. In both, nothing is created. Denied or failed do not count: whoever denied or saw it fail can try again. The comparison is by the payload's pullRequestId, across the whole project (any session).
    2. Approval. Approving a pending git_merge whose PR ANOTHER proposal already merged is 409 pr_ja_mergeado, before any effect, and the action stays pending for whoever sees it to deny. A merely LIVE sibling does not prevent deciding this one.
    3. Provider. LocalGitProvider refuses to merge an already merged PR with GitPullRequestAlreadyMergedError, and the target does not move — aligned with GitHub, which refuses the repeated merge.
    4. A pending gate is a NOTICE, never a refusal (owner decision, 09/30). The PRs tab and the chat's "Mergear" say in TEXT which gate is missing (qa-verificada with awaiting_qa or a gate not yet opened, secops-segura with awaiting_secops), and the button and the card stay active. awaiting_user, a done task and a PR without a task give no notice. The "blocked gate" (task blocked) stays as it was.
    5. No ceiling moves. Merge into a protected branch remains unconditional, human require_approval (RN-418, decide.ts): this rule only prevents proposing or approving when there is nothing to merge. Declared: two simultaneous proposals of the same PR are not serialized (there is no per-PR lock), and it is rule 2 that holds the second one.

    RN-665 — O custo real que o provider devolve é o número do metering; o catálogo fica onde ele não vem

    Decisão do dono (30/09): o custo real vira o número. Quando a resposta de uma chamada de LLM diz quanto o provider cobrou — no OpenRouter, usage.cost no frame final do stream —, esse valor é o token_usage.cost_micros da linha, o que o turno devolve ao engine (e o laço soma ao orçamento local), o que incrementa os budgets de projeto, sessão e área, e o que os relatórios de gasto somam. Sem ele, o preço congelado do catálogo produz o número, como no ADR 0042.

    1. Uma regra, três caminhos. RunLlmTurnUseCase, StreamLlmTurnUseCase e SendChatMessageUseCase passam pela mesma custoDaChamada; não há segunda régua.
    2. Preço implícito, marcado. Com custo real, as duas colunas de preço gravam custo ÷ tokens (o mesmo valor: o provider devolve UM custo) e price_implicit = true — o que mantém tokens × preço = custo (RN-044) sem fingir um preço de tabela. Sem custo real, price_implicit = false e as colunas são as do catálogo.
    3. O catálogo ao lado. catalog_cost_micros grava o que o preço de catálogo teria cobrado, só nas linhas cujo número é o real (null nas outras) — é a distância entre estimativa e fatura, por linha.
    4. estimated segue falando dos TOKENS (RN-041). A linha com custo real tem estimated = false porque o custo só chega com o usage do provider; quem marca o CUSTO como real é price_implicit.
    5. O que a resposta disse sobre si é gravado. resolved_model_name (o model do frame — o alias resolvido) e generation_id (o id, gen-… no OpenRouter), por todo provider do dialeto. model_name continua sendo o do catálogo, a dimensão dos relatórios.
    6. Só quem provou lê o custo. O hook extrairCustoReal existe só no OpenRouter; provider sem ele ignora um usage.cost presente. Custo que não é número finito e não negativo é "não disse" (zero de verdade é custo real), e com is_byok: true o custo NÃO é lido: é a taxa do hub, e a inferência é cobrada por fora — a linha cai no catálogo.

    RN-666 — O metering grava quanto da entrada veio de cache e quanto da saída foi raciocínio

    Cada linha de token_usage grava duas PARTES que o provider informa no usage do dialeto OpenAI: cached_input_tokens (prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens — quantos dos input_tokens foram servidos de cache, cobrados a uma fração do preço) e reasoning_tokens (completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens — quantos dos output_tokens foram raciocínio).

    1. Parte, nunca soma. input_tokens/output_tokens continuam sendo os totais que o provider disse, e já incluem as partes; nada é somado a eles e nenhum custo é recalculado por elas — o número do custo é o da RN-665.
    2. "Não disse" não é zero. null = o provider não informou; 0 = informou que não houve. Valor que não é inteiro não negativo é "não disse".
    3. A medição diz quanto foi cache. medir-execucao.ts passa a mostrar, por agente, o cache lido e o raciocínio com a porcentagem do total, SÓ sobre as chamadas que informaram (e em quantas, quando não foram todas), e "não medido" quando nenhuma informou — além de em quantas chamadas o custo é o real.
    4. Lido para todo provider do dialeto, porque os dois campos são da própria OpenAI; quem não os manda fica com null. O Anthropic informa cache no protocolo dele (cache_read_input_tokens) e isso NÃO é lido aqui — fica null, declarado; o Ollama não informa.

    RN-669 — The path scope compares against the REAL execution folder: /work and the container's /tmp when it is up

    The scope ceiling of ADR 0055 compared every command with the project folder on the HOST, including when the command runs INSIDE the container (RN-492/RN-502). In the real use of 09/29, the 37 "scope" requests were /work/... and /tmp compared with /home/<usuario>/projetos-brabo/<projeto> (AT-258).

    With a REGISTERED running container in a container or mounted project, the scope root is /work — the mount point, where the folder and the project's .worktrees live — plus the container's OWN /tmp. The cwd arrives as a host path and is translated to /work by the same engine rule (cwd_para_container/2): the root becomes /work, what is under it becomes /work/..., what is outside stays as it came and remains outside. In mounted the translation is bijective. Without a container, the root is still the project folder on the host, and the host's /tmp stays OUTSIDE.

    It applies to whoever is not on autopilot (the specific terminal rule): the autopilot does not go through the scope (RN-603, kept by RN-670). projectScopeRoot does not change nor merge with permissionsFilePath (RN-478); the auto-approval FLOOR remains only for container mode (RN-493). runner stays out, on purpose: the api does not know whether the runner will route to the container or to the host (RN-558). A command argument with a HOST path now counts as outside when there is a container — the engine translates only the cwd, and inside the container that path does not exist.

    RN-670 — Auto mode is the AUTOPILOT, and "Sempre permitir" does not switch it off

    Owner decision of 10/01 (ADR 0189): RN-603 is NOT revoked. The wildcard *: auto_approve approves EVERYTHING, including the synthesized compound of permissions.json, paths outside the folder, git commit and creating a LOCAL branch. Still out, never auto-approvable: push/PR/merge/deploy through the terminal and sudo/doas (RN-418), merge into a protected branch, container_remove, instruction_patch and parallelism. An explicit deny wins, and an ask written in the file asks. The guarantee that this does not reach the Brabo's code is the container's containment — a single folder, at /work, strictly below the broker's root, without the Docker socket or privilege —, proven in apps/broker/src/contencao-do-brabo.spec.ts; what the proof does NOT cover is declared in ADR 0189.

    "Sempre permitir" does not switch off the autopilot (AT-255). The dev agent click records terminal: auto_approve (RN-509), and the repository returned that specific one BEFORE the wildcard, with origin especifica — decide() stopped recognizing auto mode (97 + 37 requests in the real use of 09/29, with the mode lit on screen). Now the specific auto_approve under the wildcard auto_approve resolves as the WILDCARD. A specific one that says something else (require_approval, deny) still wins, and with the toggle back in manual the specific one recorded by the click applies alone again, with the scope. The click still records the specific one; what decides whether it already exists is the especifica field of the resolution, never the resolved mode.

    The screen says what the autopilot unlocks and what it does not, with ONE list in the three places where the mode is switched on: the Executores batch card (RN-661, open), the ApprovalCard and the toggle of the agent card (collapsed). The "does not unlock" is the text RN-661 already had, reused.

    RN-671 — The Infra starts the container on handoff acceptance: the server proposes, and the seeded autonomy approves

    Owner decision on 10/01 (ADR 0190), revising the "never seeded" of RN-491. In the real use of 09/29 the Infra announced the start "in parallel" and did not propose it; the container only started through /containers (AT-260).

    1. The seed. Accepting the handoff addressed to infra records, besides open_infra_pr: auto_approve and terminal: deny, the autonomy container_start: auto_approve. Only that one among the container ones: container_start_via_runner and container_stop remain never seeded, and container_remove remains in the absolute ceiling (RN-495).
    2. The trigger is the SERVER's. In the Infra Lead's kickoff, BEFORE the first trip to the model, if there is a current routing (artifact.module_routing roteado, with a candidate) and a container/mounted project, the server proposes container_start through the SAME path as the propose_container_start tool: the local refusals by mode and state (RN-566, RN-610), then propose_action, where the api refuses without a broker (RN-591), resolves the autonomy and, auto-approved, executes the start, electing the image through DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase with decidedBy: 'infra-lead' (RN-491). runner has no server step: it goes through container_start_via_runner, proposed by the model and decided by a human.
    3. The election is deterministic. The candidate with the most modules; on a tie, the routing's first. Network none, default resources, and a rationale that says it was the server. (Revised by RN-683: the resources are omitted and the api starts with the minimum derived from the module_map, not with the default.)
    4. The trail says who called. Durable tool.call (with origem: "servidor") and tool.result, and no tool message in the model's history; the kickoff says in text what HAS ALREADY happened (returned status, or the refusal reason).
    5. The closing of RN-668 stays true. The server's start marks the turn as the tool's would: proposed, the closing says nothing; refused, it says it was refused. A proposal DENIED by the policy (status denied, like a session opened by someone who is not maintainer) counts as a refusal, in both origins.

    No ceiling moves: the minimum role stays maintainer (the effective one of whoever opened the session), a deny in permissions.json still wins, and /containers does not change (it proposes as a human, and agent autonomy does not apply to it). Declared: the card's manual/auto toggle writes the wildcard, and the specific rule wins — putting the Infra in "manual" does not switch off this seed.

    RN-672 — The handoff to the Dev Lead comes from the Infra, and only with the project container running

    Owner decision on 10/01 (ADR 0190, AT-262). Until now "Confirmar arquitetura pronta" offered TWO handoffs — to the Infra and to the Dev Lead (FASE 14d, handoff-duplo in docs/fluxo.yml) —, and the Dev Lead could be accepted before the container in which the dev agents work existed (RN-502). In the real use of 09/29 both were born from the same confirmation (session be70, seq 252/254).

    1. The architecture confirmation offers only to the Infra. OfferInfraHandoffUseCase has one target (infra); the engine port's offerDevHandoff, the route POST /internal/sessions/:id/agent/offer-dev-handoff and the Arquiteto's :offer_dev_handoff/handoff_dev_pendente ceased to exist. ja_oferecido now means "the Infra already had an offer or was active".
    2. The one who offers the Dev Lead is the Infra Lead's server, through create_handoff_if_absent/5 (infra → dev-lead, ADR 0182): a pending offer in any session of the project comes back as is, and an already active Dev Lead (409 agente_ja_ativo) is not a failure. It is not a tool: the model does not decide when the Dev Lead comes in.
    3. Only with the container REGISTERED running (the local read of ProjectContainerLifecycle). The question is asked at two moments: at the end of every Infra turn (concluir) — the common case, because the server's start on acceptance (RN-671) runs inside the kickoff — and when the outbox's container.running arrives outside a turn (later approval, /containers, container_start_via_runner): Engine.Outbox.Drain now also enqueues Engine.Workers.InfraOfereceDevLeadWorker, which notifies the project's Infra Lead through PubSub.
    4. A failure that is not "already handled" is a durable agent.error with origin (RN-116), without bringing the turn down; the end of the Infra's next turn tries again.

    What stays as it was: the second repository door on acceptance to the Dev Lead (RN-582) — the acceptance is the same, only who offers changed — and the execution activation chained to the acceptance (RN-161). Declared: the outbox notice is at-most-once, like Engine.Dev.Wake; without an Infra Lead up at that instant, the offer waits for the end of its next turn.

    RN-675 — "Sempre permitir" records VERB + SUBCOMMAND, one pattern per command segment

    Owner decision of 10/01 (AT-257, which closes AT-170 — point 6 of ADR 0055, the unit of generalization; ADR 0189). Until now the click recorded the WHOLE command, byte for byte (Terminal(<comando>)): the next command was almost never the same — 173 clicks in the real use of 09/29 —, and the compound became ONE pattern whose content only matched the FIRST segment, so cd src && npm test only freed cd src.

    Now each SEGMENT of the command (the same cut as decide(): &&, ||, ;, |, &) becomes a pattern, and the unit is:

    • the verb alone (ls) → the verb;
    • verb + word (npm test, git status, mix test, npx vitest) → both. A "word" starts with a letter, without /, ., =, glob or flag; an argument that looks like a word (cd src) stays as a subcommand — the NARROW side of the doubt, because telling the two apart would require a list of verbs, which is the space that findings Z/AD say does not converge;
    • verb + argument that is not a word (cat src/x.ts, cd ../lib) → the verb;
    • verb + FLAG (ls -la src, git -C /x status) → the EXACT segment: the form with a flag is where verb and invocation diverge, and generalizing there would be choosing a form from within the code;
    • a unit that is a PREFIX of an RN-418 ceiling (git remote, gh pr) → the EXACT segment; and if even the exact one is a prefix (git alone), no pattern for that segment.

    Matching is still the usual one (token prefix), a click on a command with an external or privileged effect is still refused whole beforehand (motivoDeRecusaDoSempreAprovar, 400 teto_do_sempre_permitir), the decide() ceiling runs after the file, and the path scope still limits WHERE outside the autopilot (RN-669). Whoever can record is whoever already could (the endpoint's role, unchanged); the precedence with auto mode is that of RN-670. A module dev agent's "Sempre permitir" still goes to agent_autonomy (RN-509), without a pattern. Only the patterns that are MISSING are recorded and narrated; permission.granted carries patterns (the recorded list) and pattern (the same list joined by comma, for the timeline).

    RN-677 — Accepting the Dev Lead only brings him in to plan; APPROVING his plan is what activates execution

    Revises RN-161 (owner decision, 10/01): accepting the handoff to the Dev Lead no longer chains POST .../execution/activate, for EVERY role. The explicit "Ativar execução" shortcut of the card (RN-137) and the Visão Geral one remain — they are a click of their own, not the acceptance.

    The real use of 09/29 measured the inversion: execution was activated on handoff acceptance at 06:45:01 — the web chained the activation for maintainer/owner (session-acoes-de-handoff.ts, RN-161) —, and the Dev Lead's plan, proposed at 06:47:47, stayed pending and was never used. The plan had no consumer: propose_execution_plan had no execution pipeline and, approved, stayed approved forever. Measured on dev before changing: the acceptance backend (AcceptHandoffUseCase) NEVER emitted execution.activated; the only emitter is ActivateExecutionUseCase, called only by the execution/activate route.

    The rule:

    1. Accepting the Dev Lead only activates him to plan. handleAcceptHandoff accepts and nothing more; AcceptHandoffUseCase does not change — it keeps provisioning the repository as the idempotent second door (RN-582).
    2. Approving propose_execution_plan ACTIVATES execution. The action gained an executor in the api, ExecuteExecutionPlanUseCase, called by manual approval (ApproveActionUseCase) and by auto-approval (ProposeActionUseCase — the type is not in the absolute ceilings of decide.ts, so it CAN be configured auto-approvable). It records the tasks' module (RN-678) and calls the SAME ActivateExecutionUseCase as the button — no second yardstick: the 409 without a repository (RN-582), the 409 for execution.activated in a consultative session (RN-097) and the idempotent reactivation through findActiveExecutionSession stay there, untouched.
    3. Whoever activates is whoever APPROVED (decidedBy); on auto-approval, whoever opened the session — against whom decide() resolved the role. Both require maintainer, the same minimum as execution/activate, so resolving the effective role of the dev agents' git_* (the execution session's createdBy) does not change owner.
    4. The Dev Lead's session does NOT close (it is not passed as originSessionId, RN-135): it is there that he resumes the suspended turn and narrates the outcome.
    5. The outcome is named and durable. The action ends executed with { sessaoDeExecucao, modulos, tarefasAtribuidas } or failed with the motivo (the api's sentence, e.g. the 409 without a repository), plus the execution.plan_applied/execution.plan_failed event in the timeline. The Dev Lead reads the real outcome on resuming ("execução ATIVADA na sessão …" or "a ativação falhou: …"), never "plano registrado". Failing does not undo the approval: the human's decision is already recorded.

    RN-678 — The task belongs to a module, assigned by the Dev Lead in the plan, and only that module's dev picks it up

    In the real use of 09/29 dev-input-keyboard picked up "Implementar loop de queda automática da peça" and dev-board-engine picked up "Mapear teclas…": the task had no module, the story had several, and claimNext let any dev of any module of the story pick up any of its tasks (s.module_ids ? $1).

    The rule:

    1. The task has a module — tasks.module, nullable text (migration 0068_modulo_da_tarefa). The one who assigns it is the Dev Lead, in the execution plan: propose_execution_plan gained tarefas: [{ taskId, modulo }], and his kickoff lists the pending tasks of the PROJECT backlog with the task_id and the story's modules.
    2. The valid set is the current module_map. The api reads the plan (lerPlanoDeExecucao, a pure function) on PROPOSAL and refuses with 400 plano_de_execucao_invalido, without creating the action, when: the plan has no tarefas; a task has no taskId or is without a module; the module (of the task or of the plan) is outside the module_map; the task appears twice; or it does not exist in this project. The sentence names the task, the module and the valid modules, and goes back to the Dev Lead as a tool error (loop input, RN-163), for him to fix.
    3. Approval rereads the plan against the module_map of that moment (it may have changed): a refusal becomes failed without recording anything and without activating. Passing, the modules are recorded BEFORE the activation, so that no freshly started dev agent looks for an ownerless task.
    4. Only that module's dev picks it up. claimNext and countClaimableByModule use the SAME predicate (daTarefaDoModulo): a task with a module belongs to whoever has that module, and nobody else — the story's module_ids no longer decide. A task without a module is only claimable when the story has ONE module only, and it is the dev's: it is the only case in which "that module's dev" is not ambiguous, and it is the path of whoever activated through the Visão Geral without a plan. A task without a module of a story with several waits for the next plan.

    Left out, declared: a task created AFTER the plan is born without a module (the PO does not assign); the task.became_claimable notice is still routed by the STORY's modules (waking one extra dev picks up nothing, it only costs a query); and the plan's per-module agentes stays informative — activation starts one dev per module of the module_map, as before, and extra parallelism still goes through parallelize (RN-083).

    RN-679 — A curadoria recusa o alias de roteamento livre do OpenRouter

    Decisão do dono (01/10): o alias ~ não entra na curadoria — só modelo com upstream fixo. O alias de roteamento livre do OpenRouter (o id que começa com ~, como ~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest) "sempre redireciona para o último da família": o catálogo publica um preço de VITRINE (no uso real de 29/09, o do endpoint mais barato da família), a lista de endpoints vem vazia, e quem cobra é o upstream que atendeu. Não há upstream contra o qual o preço congelado do ADR 0042 signifique alguma coisa. A alternativa — preçar por upstream — foi recusada.

    1. A régua é do provider. ehAliasDeRoteamentoLivre é provider = 'openrouter' E nome começando com ~; o mesmo prefixo noutro provider não é alias e não recusa.
    2. Ativar recusa, com código. POST .../models/activate com isActive: true e algum alias no lote é 422 com code: "alias_de_roteamento_livre", os modelIds recusados e uma frase que os nomeia. O lote INTEIRO é recusado, como o 404 do id inexistente (RN-043): nem o modelo de upstream fixo do mesmo lote é ligado. A tela de catálogo mostra a frase da api num toast de título próprio, e casa pelo code, nunca pelo texto.
    3. O sync NÃO filtra o alias. Ele continua no catálogo — sumir dali faria o sync marcar unavailable o que já estava curado, e a cascata pularia os bindings dele em silêncio. A leitura da curadoria o MARCA: freeRoutingAlias, derivado de provider e nome na leitura, nunca gravado. A linha mostra o selo e o motivo em TEXTO antes de alguém tentar ativar.
    4. O que já estava curado segue funcionando. É mensurável (o nome com ~ na linha do OpenRouter), e a saída escolhida é a menos surpreendente: o alias ativo antes da regra continua ativo — os bindings dele seguem resolvendo, o seletor segue mostrando —, sai marcado no catálogo, e pode ser DESLIGADO. Desligado, não volta. Nada é apagado e nenhum binding é reescrito. Binding NOVO para um alias ainda ativo não é recusado aqui: a regra é da curadoria, e o binding segue a RN-043.

    RN-681 — História e regra parecidas com uma existente geram AVISO por embedding, nunca recusa; o gasto da checagem é linha própria do metering

    Depois de gravar uma história (create_story) ou uma regra de negócio (emit_artifact de business_rule), a api compara o TÍTULO dela com os das existentes do mesmo tipo no PROJETO, por cosseno entre vetores do modelo de embedding do RAG, e AVISA quando a mais próxima está a partir do limiar.

    1. Aviso, nunca recusa. O item já existe quando a checagem roda. O aviso volta ao agente no resultado da ferramenta — a frase nomeia o parecido, o id e o número — e fica no log como backlog.semantic_duplicate_warned. A duplicata EXATA continua recusada antes, pela RN-080 e pela RN-081, e por isso título normalizado igual sai da comparação.
    2. O limiar é 0,80 e é PONTO DE PARTIDA, não calibrado (ADR 0198, como os pesos do ADR 0080): os vetores reais do par do achado R e dos pares que não são duplicata não puderam ser gravados no ambiente em que a regra nasceu. A prova roda sozinha quando vetores.json for gravado; até lá ela é PULADA com aviso.
    3. Sem provider de embedding a checagem é PULADA e DITA — capability ausente, daemon fora, timeout: backlog.semantic_duplicate_check_skipped com o motivo no log e na frase ao agente. Nunca falha a emissão.
    4. O gasto entra no metering como linha própria: ator system/duplicata-semantica, provider e modelo do RAG, saída zero, preço do catálogo quando o modelo está nele. É a ÚNICA exceção ao corte do ADR 0075 — a indexação e a busca do RAG seguem fora —, e cabe porque a emissão acontece dentro de sessão.
    5. Tetos: as 100 existentes mais recentes (o resultado diz quantas de quantas quando corta) e 10 s de relógio para a checagem inteira.

    RN-682 — The consultative session without an agent asks for an agent: the composer does not send without a recipient, and the chat route refuses by name

    Until now, a message in a consultative session without an agent went to the SSE of POST .../chat (SendChatMessageUseCase), which sends to the bound model only the current text — no history, no system prompt, no tool — and records the answer with the MODEL NAME as actor. Measured in the real use of 09/29: session 5d66 answered "I have no access to previous conversations". The owner's decision (10/01) is that, without an active agent, the consultative session asks to choose an agent — the same yardstick as RN-584 (no default recipient) reaching the last case that still had one: the raw model.

    The measurement, before the fix: the chat route had ONE client, the screen (handleSend, only when there was no recipient — which, since RN-631, only happened in the consultative session without an agent: the creative one always has the Criativo as an option). The curl the seed prints is a development hint, in a creative session. The use case has a SECOND legitimate consumer: the provider smokes (*-provider.smoke.spec.ts) use it directly as an end-to-end instrument (credential → call → metering) in a session without an agent. That is why the api's refusal lives in the ROUTE, and the use case does not change.

    The rule:

    1. The screen does not send without a recipient. "Enviar" and Enter are locked with zero options, as they already were with two and no choice; the SSE branch left handleSend.
    2. The recipient line SHOWS who can be called. Without an option, the manual handoff selector (RN-440) moves into it — "Para", the list, and "Chamar" —, and the selector above disappears so there is not the same choice in two places. The list is the agents that converse (AGENTES_DE_CHAT, those the engine matches with their own clause) and that the manual handoff reaches, minus whoever already joined and minus the Criativo: the consultative session promises in its invitation that he does not join, because opening the ideation is what the creative one does (RN-097). Chamar offers the handoff; accepting it in the thread makes the agent the recipient (RN-631).
    3. The api refuses the same case for any client. POST .../chat in a consultative session in which no agent.activated was recorded is 422 {reason: "destinatario_ausente"}, with the sentence that points to .../agents/:agent/message, BEFORE any effect: nothing is recorded and no model is called. The refusal goes out as an HTTP response and not as an error frame inside a 200 stream — the handler returns Promise<Observable>, and the rejection before the SSE header becomes the normal response.

    What this rule does NOT close, declared:

    • The route still answers through the raw model outside that case: in a creative session without an agent (the seed's curl) and in a consultative one WITH an agent, for whoever calls it by hand. The screen calls it in neither; the owner's decision was about the consultative session without an agent, and closing the whole route is a separate decision.

    • Free chat with history, the other option of AT-254, was not done.

    RN-683 — The Infra starts the container with the SMALLEST eligible resource, derived from what the Arquiteto declares per module in the module_map

    Owner decision on 10/01 (ADR 0199, AT-261). Until now omitted resources became RECURSOS_PADRAO (2 cpus, 4096 MiB, 512 pids) and the server's start on acceptance (RN-671) always omitted it: every container was born at the default, with no notion of minimum.

    1. Each module declares its own. The module_map gains resources (cpus, memoryMb, pidsLimit) per module — what THAT module needs alone in the container. The create_module_map tool asks for it; the api accepts it absent and refuses with 400, on map creation: a HALF declaration (all three or none), a non-positive value or one above the ceiling, and a SUM across modules above the ceiling. The field lives in the artifact's JSON, without a migration.
    2. The minimum is the SUM, field by field. A project has ONE container (project_id UNIQUE in project_containers) and the modules run in it at the same time; the maximum across modules would undersize the container whenever two were up.
    3. A module without a declaration: floor at today's default. No number is invented. If there is a module without a declaration, the minimum is the larger of the sum of the declared ones and RECURSOS_PADRAO, field by field, and the rationale NAMES who did not declare. With no declaration at all (every map prior to this rule), and without a current module_map, the minimum is exactly today's default.
    4. The container_start execution resolves field by field. Omitted becomes the minimum (the server's start sends everything omitted); below the minimum is a named failed, without recording an image decision or starting; above is valid up to the ceiling, which does not change. The rationale of the recorded artifact.project_image gains "Recursos mínimos (RN-683): …" with the summed modules and the map version.
    5. A single yardstick. The api derives; the engine sums nothing and the server's start says in the rationale that the resources are the derived minimum.

    Out, declared: choose_project_image (the Arquiteto decides the image and its resources) and container_start_via_runner (starts the already decided image) do not change; the refusal below the minimum happens on execution, not on proposing.

    RN-684 — The contract between modules is a versioned artifact of the Arquiteto, and the dev agent reads it through the tool, never in another dev's worktree

    Owner decision (10/01), recorded in ADR 0200. In the real use of 09/29, dev-board-engine spent 5 of its 24 tool steps reading other modules' worktrees to discover their interface: the module_map says who depends on whom, never what a module exposes. It applies RN-164 to the dev agents.

    1. The artifact is artifact.module_contracts, without a table, like module_routing and c4_diagram: the current one is the highest version, with ties broken by seq. Each declaration carries the WHOLE list and REPLACES the previous one; changing a contract is a new version by the Arquiteto.
    2. Per module, only what it EXPOSES: {modulo, expoe: [{tipo, assinatura, descricao}]}, tipo in funcao | rota | evento | dado, assinatura mandatory (up to 300 characters), from 1 to 40 items. What it CONSUMES is the dependsOn of the current module_map, derived on read — never retyped.
    3. The api refuses with 400 and the whole reason (which goes back to the model, RN-061): empty list, repeated module, module outside the current module_map (listing the valid ones) or no module_map, empty expoe or above 40, unknown tipo, empty assinatura or above 300. Nothing is recorded.
    4. An artifact SEPARATE from the module_map, never a field of it: revising one does not reissue the other.
    5. The dev reads through listar_contratos_de_modulos, :direct, in the Engine.Dev.Tools registry: project scope by the route, NO parameter, the dev's module coming from ctx.module. It shows in full its own and those it consumes; those that consume it and the rest, by name only; a ceiling of 120 items with the cut stated. A contract of a module that left the map is STATED, never attributed.
    6. The dev's kickoff says where to read another module's interface, and that it is not in another dev agent's worktree. Without a contract for a shown module, the tool says to implement from what the story and the task say and, if an interface is missing, report_blocked naming the module — never rereading the worktree.

    RN-685 — Revoking a credential brings down only the connections opened WITH IT: the socket ticket keeps the credential, and the target stops being {project, user}

    Revises RN-520. Until now, revoking a device key brought down the runner's live connection by the {project, user} pair, because the credential's identity died in PatAuthGuard: a runner of the SAME user connected with a PAT or with another key went down too, and the MACHINE key (RN-543) multiplied that per project. Revoking a PAT brought down nothing.

    The ticket keeps WHICH credential requested it. runner_socket_tickets (an engine table) gains credential_kind (device_key | pat) and credential_id (the kid, which is the record's id — RN-475 —, or the PAT's id), both NULLABLE: the terminal ticket belongs to the web tab and has no device credential, and a runner one issued by an older api arrives without it. The PatAuthGuard annotates the credential AFTER authorizing (request.credencialDeDispositivo), the runner ticket carries it to the engine and the terminal one never does; an incomplete pair or an unknown kind becomes ABSENT, never an invented credential.

    The socket keeps the credential, and its id too. connect/3 sets assigns.credencial, and the id becomes runner_socket:<kind>:<projectId>:<userId>:<espécie>:<id> when it exists — the disconnect the channel broadcasts to its own id reaches only that credential.

    Revoking ONE credential:

    1. voids its PENDING tickets — a request made seconds before the revocation does not get in after it (consumed_at, the same "already used" state, no new state);
    2. asks EVERY runner in the cluster whether it was born from this credential — only the channel knows —, and only those born from it go down. The machine key is ONE request, and goes down in every project where it opened a connection, including one the api would not list;
    3. responds with a TALLY (derrubados, legados, intocados, semResposta, ticketsAnulados) — zero brought down is the normal case for an orphan key (RN-519).

    It applies to the three revocations: the key one (per project and through the Account, RN-611) and the two PAT ones (the owner's, RN-426, and the maintainer's, RN-427). It revokes FIRST, brings down afterwards, and bringing down is still a side effect that only LOGS — the DELETE stays 204 and idempotent.

    What already went down still goes down (the prohibition of AT-013). The LEGACY connection — a ticket without a credential — of the same owner, in one of the projects that a KEY revocation sends as scope (the row's, or the machine's candidates), goes down by the pair as before; the PAT gains no legacy scope, because it brought down nothing. And if the engine does not know the per-credential route (404 from an older engine), the key revocation falls back to the pair, disconnectRunnerOfUser, project by project.

    The {project, user} pair remains, with another owner: it is the target of member removal (RN-615), which removes the PERSON, with whatever credential.

    The screen states the precision (RN-561): the revoke confirmation — device keys in Configurações and machine keys in the Account — replaces "outro runner seu também cai" with "só cai o que se conectou com ESTA chave". The label changes, not the behavior.

    The RN-418 ceiling also applies through the typed door (RN-689)

    RN-689 — Typed git_push and pr_open are never auto-approvable: the RN-418 ceiling applies to the command AND to the action

    Revised by RN-713 (AT-385, 10/02): auto mode (the wildcard in auto_approve) now unlocks git_push and pr_open.

    Revises RN-418, by owner decision (10/01). Until now decide()'s external-effect ceiling only looked at actionType === 'terminal': a TYPED git push became require_approval, and the message said to use the typed action git_push — which, with the minimum role (maintainer) met, was born auto_approved through ANY of the three stages: the "*" wildcard of auto mode (RN-153, the autopilot of RN-670), a specific agent_autonomy rule (execution activation seeded git_push/pr_open as auto_approve for each dev-<modulo>) or an allow in permissions.json. Measured in decide.spec.ts before the fix: the six cases (two types × three stages) came out auto_approve.

    The rule: git_push and pr_open enter the block of absolute ceilings — if the verdict up to that point is auto_approve, it becomes unconditional require_approval, with the named reason ("teto de efeito externo (RN-418): … nunca é auto-aprovável"), which goes in proposed_action.created. deny has already returned before and still wins; the ORIGIN of the autonomy does not matter. The "sempre permitir" of both was already refused at the source (RN-642, TIPOS_SEM_SEMPRE_PERMITIR), and that is the half that keeps the ceiling from being decorative.

    The seeding follows along: DEV_AUTO_GIT_ACTIONS becomes only git_commit — on activation and on parallelization acceptance. Seeding push and PR would be recording an autonomy that decide() never honors, the screen promising what does not happen (the argument of RN-642). Already recorded rows stay in the database, inert. The dev agent follows the path of RN-050: commit executed, push and PR pending, agent in awaiting_approval holding the worktree until task.pr_settled; only then does the gate open.

    Left OUT, on purpose: git_merge (its own protected-branch ceiling); git_commit (stays on the machine, RN-670); open_adr_pr and open_infra_pr (they open a real PR on the provider, but the owner's decision does not cover them — open_infra_pr is seeded auto_approve on the Infra's acceptance, RN-671); the bootstrap actions (git_repo_create/git_branch_create/git_branch_protect, which do not go through decide()); and deploy, which is not a proposed_action type — it only exists as a target of the terminal command's message.

    RN-704 — The local repository's merge is a real merge, and a conflict is a named refusal

    • Rule: the local provider's mergePullRequest fast-forwards only when the target is an ancestor of the source; with the two diverged, it builds a merge commit with both parents (git merge-tree --write-tree + commit-tree, without a worktree, message Merge pull request #N from <branch>, identity Brabo Bot). The target ref is moved by update-ref with the expected old value, so a concurrent merge fails instead of overwriting. A conflict throws GitMergeConflictError with the conflicting files: the ref stays intact, the PR stays open, the git_merge action ends failed with the reason in action.failed, and over HTTP the error is 409 merge_conflict.
    • Measurement (AT-377): two PRs from the same base commit (#3 and #4) merged in sequence: dev ended up with only #4, and #3's commits stopped being its ancestors. The old update-ref was a forced reset.

    RN-715 — A merge conflict returns the task to the owning dev agent, and the gates judge again

    • Rule: when the approved merge of a PR is refused due to a conflict with dev (GitMergeConflictError, RN-704), each task of the PR that is in_review goes back to in_progress with gate_status reset (the old QA/SecOps verdicts do not apply to the branch that is going to change), records backlog.task_status_changed with cause: merge_conflict and puts task.merge_conflict in the outbox, with the agent that proposed the pr_open (the OWNER), the PR and the conflicting files. The engine delivers it to the owner through Engine.Dev.Wake; if free, he READOPTS the PR's branch (WorktreeManager.adopt/3, the same garantir_base, without losing the commits) and runs the CORRECTION loop with the reason in the text: bring in origin/dev through git fetch/git merge, resolve the files, run the suite. On report_done he proposes commit and push through the usual path (the current approval policy decides) and the gate RESTARTS from QA (open_gate + QA), without a new pr_open — the PR is the same branch. No new task state: in_progress with the cause in the event.
    • Named outcomes: owner without a row in dev_agent_states — the task is BLOCKED (conflito de merge sem dev agent para resolvê-lo, origin infra); owner with the breaker open (idle_tripped) — blocked, origin politica; the branch does not come back (adopt fails) — blocked, origin infra. A busy owner (working/awaiting_gate/awaiting_approval) gets the conflict again in 30 s. The merge refusal (RN-705) does not depend on any of this: the action is already failed, with the reason, before the engine acts. A task that is no longer in_review (repeated merge) is not reopened nor wakes anyone, and a PR opened by a human has no owner to wake.
    • Measurement (AT-383, 10/02, loja-teste): #6 ended failed due to a conflict in package.json, and the task stayed in_review with nobody to resolve it.

    RN-720 — The PO completes the story that already exists, and does not offer the handoff to the Arquiteto with an uncovered rule

    Context: in the real use of loja-teste-2 (10/02) the PO created twelve stories without a linked rule, read in listar_regras_de_negocio that seven of the eight rules were WITHOUT coverage, wrote that it had no tool to edit a story and called offer_handoff to the Arquiteto anyway — asserting in the thread that coverage was complete and that the system would accept on its own. The automatic acceptance of RN-660 did not happen (the criterion did not hold), and the story it recreated triggered the semantic duplicate notice (RN-681).

    The rule:

    1. The PO has complete_story: it completes an EXISTING draft story of the project — the given business_rule_ids are ADDED to those already linked (completing never unlinks a rule; an id that is not an artifact.business_rule is 400), given non-empty lists replace the current ones and omitted ones stay. A story that is not draft is 409; from another project, 404. After writing, promotion follows the SAME criterion as create_story (isPromotable; auto goes to ready, manual sets proposedReady), and the write records backlog.story_completed.
    2. The PO's offer_handoff to the Arquiteto is REFUSED, without creating an offer, while there is a rule without a story or an incomplete draft story (without proposedReady) — and the result lists both, with id and title, and says to complete with complete_story. Coverage is the api's (computeCoverage, the same as the automatic acceptance), never a second count in the engine; a read failure does not become a refusal. The other agents and targets do not go through the check.
    3. When the PO's business_rule emit_artifact comes back with the similarity notice (status: warned), the result adds that the rule seems to ALTER an existing one and that it should ask the user (ask_structured_questions) which one holds before going on (AT-389: the user said "taxa fixa de R$ 10", the Criativo recorded "R$ 10 por pedido" and the PO emitted "R$ 10 por torrefador"). The already recorded rule is not undone; the notice stays a notice.

    The PO's kickoff says all three things.

    RN-727 — The draft story is corrected and archived, by the PO and by the user, without deleting anything

    • Rule: a draft story WITHOUT a task in execution (in_progress or in_review) can have its title corrected and can be ARCHIVED — by the PO (tools update_story, which also corrects the description, and archive_story) and by the user in the Backlog tab ("Editar título" and "Arquivar", with confirmation). Both doors go through the SAME yardstick (recusaDeCorrecaoDeHistoria), and the refusal is a NAMED 409: historia_arquivada, historia_nao_draft or historia_com_tarefa_em_execucao, with the sentence the model and the toast show. Archiving does NOT delete: the stories row gets archived_at/archived_reason (migration 0069, ADR 0212), the tasks stay, and the NEW event backlog.story_archived keeps who, why and which tasks; the edit records backlog.story_updated with the previous title. The archived story leaves the backlog (listar_backlog included — the PO does not see it so as not to complete it again), the coverage (computeCoverage reads only the non-archived ones), the promotion queue, the Dev Lead's plan and the claim, and its tasks go with it, through the story; transition, complete_story and create_task refuse an archived story. The user's minimum role is that of the other backlog writes (promote/return, RN-048): developer; below it the buttons stay inert with the reason in text, and the same applies to a story outside draft or with a task in execution. Each story shows how many tasks it has.

    RN-734 — The OpenAI-compatible path ALWAYS sends the output ceiling

    • Rule: every chat call through the /chat/completions dialect (the providers born from OpenAICompatibleProvider, OpenRouter included) carries the output ceiling field — max_tokens or max_completion_tokens, according to maxTokensField — even when the caller does not set maxTokens. The reason is the credit RESERVATION: without the field, OpenRouter reserves per call the model's MAXIMUM output and refuses with 402 ("would exceed your available credits given your current in-flight requests") with a balance that would cover the real call. Today no caller (engine → llm-turn) sets maxTokens, so the default applies to all agents. An answer cut by the ceiling (finish_reason: "length") is read and narrated since RN-737 (RN-698 narrates the ITERATION ceiling, not the token one). Hypothesis NOT measured with a real key: that the reservation explains TP-01's 402.

    RN-761 — An installed dependency does not enter the repository: base .gitignore, a commit that excludes it and a gate that flags it

    • Rule: three layers, with the SAME list of directories (node_modules, deps, _build, .venv, venv, __pycache__, vendor, target):
      1. the repository bootstrap (the three providers and adoption) gets the commit_gitignore step, which commits a base .gitignore to main BEFORE dev is born, so every working branch inherits it. It is the single point because it is through it that EVERY created or adopted repository passes, before any agent writes; the Infra through the module_map would arrive after the dev's first commit and only in the projects that go through it. The step only CREATES the file: an already existing .gitignore, even a different one, is the user's and does not enter the plan;
      2. the dev agent's commit (git_commit) and the commit that preserves the worktree on blocking (RN-743) stage everything EXCEPT those directories, at any depth (pathspec :(exclude,glob)), even without a .gitignore;
      3. the SecOps gate flags, as a finding (changes_requested), a directory from the list that appears in the PR's diff, with the file count. The two copies of the list (api and engine) are checked by test. Declared: a dependency file ALREADY tracked before this rule is not removed by the commit (the exclusion does not stage removal); an already bootstrapped project only gets the .gitignore if the bootstrap runs again; in runner mode the commit runs through the same GitExecutor and the same exclusion applies where the engine runs git.

    RN-802 — A estimativa do plano do Dev Lead soma o dobro da primeira tarefa de cada módulo

    O cartão de aprovação do propose_execution_plan (RN-709) dizia "até N × teto", ignorando que a primeira tarefa de cada módulo tem o dobro do teto (RN-774). Agora a api leva no payload, ao lado de orcamentoPorTarefaMicros, o multiplicadorDaPrimeiraDoModulo, e a frase soma o teto EFETIVO: (tarefas − módulos com tarefa) × teto + módulos com tarefa × multiplicador × teto, dizendo "a primeira de cada módulo vale o dobro". Com 8 tarefas num módulo e teto de US$ 0,50: até US$ 4,50. É limite superior: a primeira de um módulo que já teve tarefa reivindicada não ganha o dobro, e a frase continua dizendo "até". Sem o multiplicador no payload (proposta antiga), a conta antiga.

    O multiplicador é APLICADO só no engine (Engine.Dev.TetoDaTarefa); a api tem um espelho declarado, porque a tela não deve copiar a constante e o engine não é consultado na proposta. Mudar um exige mudar o outro.

    RN-847 — A merged PR keeps stating the files it changed

    • Rule: extension of RN-844. In the LOCAL git provider, the diff of a PR was target...source also after the merge — and then the merge base is the source's own tip, so the merged PR returned ZERO files (measured in a test: [] for fast-forward and for a merge commit), and the "Contexto da sessão" panel said "Nenhum arquivo nas PRs" with 14 merged PRs, with nothing in prsNaoLidas (the diff did not fail, it came empty). Now the merge records in the PR's store the merge base and the source tip at the moment of the merge (mergedBaseSha/mergedHeadSha), and the merged PR's diff is mergedBaseSha...mergedHeadSha. A PR merged before those fields falls back to the target's merge commit (first parent) whose second parent is the source tip; one merged by fast-forward without the fields cannot be reconstructed and stays empty (declared gap). GitHub and GitLab already return the merged PR's diff through the platform itself. On screen, the context summary is reread on the SAME triggers that reread the PR list (RN-841): the channel's prs target (with its 2 s window, no extra fetch) and the change of the backlog signature, by prefix ['session-context-summary', projectId].

    RN-858 — An agent's open question is a durable record, and only the session author answers it

    • Rule: the doubt an agent leaves for the user becomes the artifact.open_question event (append-only, in the log of the session where it is born) with {questionId (uuid), pergunta (até 500), sugestao (até 300, opcional), afeta: {regras, historias, tarefas}, autor, sessionId} — the events funnel refuses with 400 a payload outside that shape, whether it comes from the engine or the api. It closes with open_question.answered {questionId, resposta, aceitouSugestao, decisionEventId, respondidaPor}; the STATUS comes from the log (open = without answered), never from a table. GET /projects/:projectId/open-questions?status=open|answered|all (viewer, default open) lists the most recent first, with a ceiling of 50 and the total (RN-180), and states in autorDaSessao who can answer. POST .../open-questions/:questionId/answer with {resposta} or {aceitarSugestao: true} is only accepted from the AUTHOR of the originating session (403 so_o_autor_da_sessao); already answered is 409 pergunta_ja_respondida, a question from another project is 404 and an empty answer (or a suggestion that does not exist) is 400. Answering records, in one transaction, an artifact.decision_record with the user as actor (context = the question, choice = the answer, consequences = what it affects, plus questionId and afeta) and the open_question.answered, notifies the session channel (through the funnel, RN-579) and asks the engine to resume the PARKED QA gate of each affected task (the RN-724 path) — best effort: a gate that was not parked or an engine that is down does not undo the answer. ADR 0214.

    RN-860 — The QA gate waits for the user without spending the correction cycle

    RN-892 — O prefixo estável da chamada vai marcado para o cache de prompt, e a capability é ligada só no OpenRouter, provada

    Medido no TP-01 (15/10): o anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 pelo OpenRouter recebeu 8,40 M tokens de entrada com 0 em cache, e a entrada foi US$ 0,84 dos US$ 1,02. Modelos Anthropic só leem do cache o prefixo marcado com cache_control: { type: "ephemeral" } num bloco de conteúdo de texto (até quatro pontos, TTL de 5 min — https://openrouter.ai/docs/features/prompt-caching).

    1. Capability de provider, obrigatória. LLMProviderCapabilities.promptCaching é true só no OpenRouter e false nos outros oito. Declará-la sem o hook marcarCacheDePrompt falha na construção. Desligada, o corpo é byte a byte o de antes.
    2. Camada de modelo na config. No OpenRouter só anthropic/* recebe ponto; os demais cacheiam sozinhos e voltam intactos.
    3. Dois pontos, sobre o que não muda. A última system do prefixo (instruções, e as ferramentas antes delas) e a última user/tool antes da cauda de system do fim. A cauda — idioma (RN-622), ambiente (RN-706), fluxo (RN-711), perfil (RN-680) — fica DEPOIS do último ponto, e a ordem das mensagens nunca muda.
    4. Prova (ADRs 0041/0042). Em 2026-10-15 o smoke rodou com credencial real (OPENROUTER_TEST_KEY=… pnpm --filter api exec vitest run test/infrastructure/llm/openrouter-provider.cache.smoke.spec.ts) e a segunda chamada a anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 voltou com cached_input_tokens=8011; só então a capability do OpenRouter passou a true. Ligar outro provider exige o smoke equivalente. O ganho aparece no metering pela RN-666.
    • Código: apps/api/src/infrastructure/llm/openrouter-provider.ts:276 (marcarCacheDePromptOpenRouter); apps/api/src/infrastructure/llm/openai-compatible-provider.ts:501 (mensagens)

The /containers page gains decisaoVigente and imagemDesatualizada per row — the divergence compares CONTENT (image, network, resources), never the version number, because the Infra election writes v+1 with the same content on every start — and, with a diverging running/stopped/provisioning container, the row says in text "Stop → Remove → Start again" and says why "Start again" does not apply the new image.     • Origin: AT-595 (TP-01 20th: the v3 egress decision did not reach the v2 none container and the Image column stayed on v2)

    RN-906 — The API refuses network none when a module's stack downloads dependencies

    • Rule: when deciding the project image, if the network is none and any module of the current module_map has a stack that matches, as a whole word, the closed list of ecosystems that download dependencies (node, npm, pnpm, yarn, python, pip, elixir, mix, go, rust, cargo, ruby, java, maven, gradle, php, dotnet...), the API answers 400 naming the module, the stack and the term, and asks for egress. Nothing is written and the network is never switched on its own: egress is the user's authorization. It applies to the Architect (choose_project_image) and to the Infra election, which go through the same use case (for Infra, container_start ends failed with the reason, without calling the broker). With no module_map, or a stack that does not match, only the RN-735 warning remains. No configurable exception. Revises RN-735 (warning → refusal in that case).
    • Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/containers/decidir-imagem-do-projeto.use-case.ts:80 (stackQueBaixaDependencias)
    • Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/containers/container-do-projeto.use-case.spec.ts; apps/api/test/domain/containers/project-container.spec.ts; apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/execute-container-start.use-case.spec.ts
    • Origin: AT-593 (EP-031).

    RN-909 — 9Router is the 10th provider: per-installation URL, mandatory credential, public price curated

    • Rule: the 9router provider talks to a gateway on the owner's machine. The base URL is NINE_ROUTER_BASE_URL (default http://host.docker.internal:20128/v1), read on each use by the provider and by the connection test (GET /models with the key). The credential is mandatory. The provider capabilities are false (only listModels and streaming, required by the contract, are true) until a smoke with a key proves the rest (ADR 0041). Model prices are not discovered: they enter by manual curation and, by the owner's decision, a subscription model records the equivalent API's public price, not zero. The provider sends x-9router-token-saver: off on every call, so 9Router does not compress the tool_result.
    • Where: apps/api/src/infrastructure/llm/nine-router-provider.ts:83 (nineRouterConfig)
    • Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/llm/nine-router-provider.contract.spec.ts:109 (capabilities, URL from the environment, header, connection test, synthetic fixture parse); manual smoke in nine-router-provider.smoke.spec.ts.
    • Origin: AT-576a (EP-026), ADR 0222, owner's decision of 22/10.

    RN-910 — The default ceiling per area is 5 in dev, 4 in qa and 2 in infra

    Each agent area is born with a parallelism ceiling that comes from the catalog: dev 5, qa 4, infra 2 (AT-599, owner's request of 22/10). Migration 0073 applied the same values to all existing projects, overwriting what had already been decided — the owner's decision, taken knowing that a ceiling set on purpose is lost.

    • Today only the dev ceiling is applied at execution. RequestParallelizationUseCase reads the dev area when deciding parallelism. qa and infra have the value stored, shown and editable, but no code consults it: raising their ceiling changes no execution at all.
    • The dev ceiling only bites with 3 modules or more. The maximum number of dev agents is one per module plus one extra (dev-<modulo>-2), that is, 2 × modules (RN-083). With 2 modules the maximum is 4, below 5.
    • Only the INSERT uses the catalog value. Seeding again does not touch the row (RN-094). The column stays default(2): that value only appears in a raw INSERT, outside the use case.
    • Where: apps/api/src/domain/agents/agent-areas.ts:73 (maxParallelPadrao); apps/api/src/application/use-cases/agents/seed-agent-areas.use-case.ts:53 (maxParallelAoNascer); apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/agent-area.repository.ts:62 (nascer); apps/api/src/application/use-cases/execution/request-parallelization.use-case.ts:13 (MAX_PARALLEL_PADRAO); migration apps/api/src/db/migrations/0073_paralelismo_padrao_por_area.sql.
    • Test: test/application/use-cases/iam/create-project-semeia-areas.spec.ts (a new project is born with 5/4/2), test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/agent-area.repository.spec.ts (seeding again does not undo the altered ceiling), test/db/paralelismo-padrao-migration.spec.ts (rows with 2, 3 and 7 end at 5/4/2) and test/application/use-cases/execution/request-parallelization.use-case.spec.ts (the default of 5 decides the dev's parallelism).
